articleTitle: Spacecraft Attitude Tracking Control Based On High-Order Fully Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the attitude tracking control of spacecraft. Firstly, the modified Rodrigues parameters are selected to characterize the spacecraft’s attitude, whose mathematical model is then established by considering the uncertainties of the spacecraft parameters and the bounded disturbances. The mathematical model of the spacecraft is transformed into a type of high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system with uncertainties. Then, based on the HOFA system approach, a robust controller for a type of HOFA system with uncertainties is designed, which can ensure that the system states converge to an arbitrary ellipsoidal region. Finally, the validness of the designed controller is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Robust Fault-Tolerant Control for Uncertain High-Order Fully Actuated Systems with Actuator Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault-tolerant controller for a class of uncertain high-order fully actuated systems (FASs) with actuator faults. Recently, the FAS approaches have been rapidly developed in different fields. In order to cope with the fault tolerance issue for actuators in FAS framework, a multiplicative fault gain is introduced to the basic uncertain high-order system. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, a full-state feedback strategy is presented to ensure the globally uniformly asymptotically (GUA) stability of the considered FAS. Additionally, in the absence of actuator faults, the proposed fault-tolerant controller can robustly stabilize the FASs. A numerical experiment illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Coordinated control of distributed multi-agent systems using event-triggered predictive control strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the coordinated control problem for a class of distributed networked multi-agent systems (NMASs) is studied. An event-triggered predictive coordinated control (ETPCC) scheme is proposed to compensate for the communication delay between controllers as well as to reduce the communication frequency. With the aim of reducing the frequency of data transfer among controllers and saving resources, a distributed event-triggered condition is designed to decide when to transfer information. Further, a cost function using predicted values is proposed to measure the cooperative performance among the agents, and the required control increment for each agent is obtained by minimizing the cost function. Simulation and experimental examples show that the proposed ETPCC strategy works effectively.

articleTitle: Robust Stabilization Control for High-order Sub-fully Actuated Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Motivated by a high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approach, this paper proposes a robust stabilization control method for a class of high-order sub-fully actuated systems (SFASs) to stabilize the system while weakening the influence of unknown nonlinear uncertainties. In comparison to most existing methods, this paper investigates the case of SFASs, allowing more sophisticated and challenging control problems to be solved due to the presence of feasibility issues. Firstly, with the assistance of concepts including the feasible set, a model for a class of uncertain high-order SFASs is proposed, representing general dynamical systems subject to unknown nonlinear uncertainties. Then, the robust stabilization control law can be directly constructed by means of the sub-full-actuation feature, which ensures that the states eventually converge asymptotically to the origin and provides a considerable amount of design degrees of freedom to allow for possible additional requirements in the application. By limiting the initial values to a restricted region, the proposed method solves the feasibility problem, which is the key to the control of SFASs, and assures that the control law always makes sense. The permanent existence of the initial values satisfying the constraint ensures that the robust stabilization control problem of the SFASs is always solvable. Finally, the power of the introduced method is illustrated by the satellite attitude control problem.

articleTitle: Fully Actuated System Based Spacecraft Attitude Finite Time Control
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of attitude stabilization control in finite time. Considering the nonlinear system under external disturbance and model uncertainty, an attitude controller based on Fully Actuated System (FAS) can be designed to compensate the nonlinearity. Compared to traditional controllers, FAS is often more immune to the nonlinear factors and its control law is easier to design. FAS compound with Fast Terminal Sliding Mode (FAFSM) is designed to guarantee the system state stable within finite time. The simulation results show that the proposed FSFSM is tolerant to the external disturbance. And it can make the dynamic response more superior with 4-5s faster convergence, which means our algorithm can achieve more quality dynamic character in finite time by comparing with single FAS controller. This explores the application in spacecraft control of FAS.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Control for Nonlinear Systems: A High-Order Full-Actuation Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel event-triggered stabilization control scheme is developed for a class of nonlinear systems in strict-feedback form. By utilizing the high-order full-actuation (HOFA) theory, an explicit design process of ideal controller is proposed for the system. Then, an actual control input based on event-sampled variables is designed to improve communication efficiency. Compared with the existing event-triggered control algorithm via the HOFA theory, the proposed control strategy can reduce the transmission frequencies of the dual channels. Meanwhile, the current state information is considered in the designed adaptive threshold which can obtain suitable triggering step sizes. Finally, by combining the impulsive dynamic analysis method and Lyapunov stability theorem, it is proved that all states of the closed-loop system are kept uniformly ultimately bounded. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is demonstrated by a simulation example.

articleTitle: High-order robust dynamic surface control for uncertain nonlinear systems based on fully actuated system approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a robust dynamic surface control method is designed for high-order strict feedback systems with nonlinear uncertainties. Based on the idea of dynamic surface control, a series of first-order low-pass filters are introduced to obtain the derivative of the virtual control law, and the controller is designed directly for each higher-order subsystem without converting it into the first-order one, hence is more concise and efficient. It is proved by the Lyapunov stability theory that the tracking error can converge to a small domain around zero. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is also verified by a simulation with the flexible joint robotic arm system.

articleTitle: A Subfully Actuated System Application: Predictive Control for Multi-RTAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: As a study of subfully actuated system applications, in this paper, the predictive control for the multiple rotational translational actuator (Multi-RTAC) system is investigated from a novel perspective. Based on the mechanism of models and state coupling relations, the connection between the fully actuated system (FAS) with the benchmark under-actuated multi-RTAC system is established. The multi-RTAC system is derived into the multi-order sub-FAS with a set of singular points. Remarkably, mathematically assigning full actuation to the under-actuated multi-RTAC system not only greatly simplifies the corresponding complex nonlinear optimization problem during the design of the predictive controller, but also defines the region of exponential attraction (ROEA) of initial values of states by the set of singular points. Meanwhile, the proposed off-line explicit analytical substabilizing predictive controller fundamentally mitigates the computational burden and guarantees the substabilization of the resultant closed-loop system in the ROEA. Finally, the simulation of the triple-RTAC system is given to demonstrate the effectiveness and simplicity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Output Tracking Based on Generalized Proportional-Integral Observer for Fully Actuated Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized proportional-integral observer for fully actuated systems. Based on the Lipschitz condition and the convexity principle, the condition expressed by the linear matrix inequality is given to ensure that the estimation error converges exponentially. Due to the full-actuation property, an observer-based output tracking controller is designed, which divides the closed-loop system into a linear constant part and a nonlinear error part. The condition for the convergence of the tracking error is also given. An example is presented to show the effect of the approach.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Fuzzy Control of Flexible-Joint Robot: A Fully Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates an adaptive event-triggered control problem for a class of flexible-joint (FJ) robot systems without converting the system into first-order systems. In order to solve the problem, fuzzy logic systems (FLSs) are introduced to deal with the unknown nonlinear functions. An adaptive event-triggered fuzzy high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system control scheme is proposed by using backstepping and event-triggered strategy. The proposed event-triggered controller guarantees that system states converge to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of origin. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is proved by FJ robot example.

articleTitle: Adaptive Disturbance Observer Design for Discrete-Time High-Order Fully Actuated Systems Based on LMI and Its Application to Combined Spacecrafts
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the design of an adaptive disturbance observer for discrete-time high-order fully actuated (HOFA) systems, with application to the combined spacecraft simulator system. Firstly, a step backward HOFA model is introduced, which accounts for input uncertainty and external disturbance. Then, an adaptive disturbance observer based control (ADOBC) is developed using Lyapunov theories, ensuring that the resulting closed-loop system is asymptotically stable and that the output of the observer can track the disturbance. The feedback control matrices and the observer gain matrices are then obtained by solving a linear matrix inequality (LMI). Finally, the proposed approach is implemented in the combined spacecraft simulator, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Control of PEMFC Air Feed Systems Via High-Order Fully Actuated System Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Oxygen excess ratio(OER) is an important indicator for proton exchange membrane fuel cell(PEMFC) air feed system, which need to be controlled at optimal point to guarantee good performance during PEMFC operation. A novel control strategy for PEMFC air feed system is proposed in this paper. The extended state observer(ESO) is designed to estimate the cathode pressure. Then the HOFAS model of PEMFC is derived from traditional state space model. And the placement of dynamic characteristics for air supply system could be realized by the parameterized controller combined with ESO. Finally the simulation case is presented, and simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of HOFAS control for air feed system.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of a 6-DOF Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A trajectory tracking controller is designed for a six-degree-of-freedom manipulator with high nonlinear and strong coupling based on a high-order fully-actuated system model. Firstly, the kinematic model and dynamic model of the six-degree-of-freedom manipulator are established by using the Modified D-H method and Lagrange dynamic equation, and the joint motor model is introduced into the system to generate a third-order dynamic model with voltage input, so as to avoid the negative impact of control for the motor itself on the tracking accuracy of the system. Then, the trajectory tracking controller is designed by direct parameterization method under the framework of high order fully-actuated system model, so that the nominal manipulator system can track the trajectory of the upper target in a finite time. Considering the internal and external uncertainty (IEU) in the practical manipulator system, a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) is designed to improve the anti-jamming ability of the system. In addition, a track-differentiator (T-D) is adopted in this paper to obtain the second stage status of the system, so as to avoid using acceleration sensors in the construction of trajectory tracking controller and nonlinear disturbance observer, which reduces the system implementation cost. Finally, a switching control strategy (SCS) is designed to improve the realization of the system due to the large output of the controller in the transient process. The effectiveness of the above theory is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Attitude Tracking Control of Rigid Spacecraft Based on Fully Actuated System Models
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a direct parametric design method for the attitude tracking control of a rigid spacecraft to address the problem of satellite attitude control performance affected by external disturbance. Firstly, the fully-actuated system model for attitude tracking control of a rigid spacecraft is established using quaternions. An extended state observer (ESO) is then developed to handle the influence caused by external disturbances. Then, a controller is designed using the direct parametric method to achieve high-accuracy attitude tracking control of the rigid spacecraft and reach the desired position. Finally, a numerical example involving a rigid spacecraft is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving the design objective and exhibiting good control performance.

articleTitle: High-Order Fully Actuated System Models for Discrete-Time Strict-Feedback Systems with Increasing Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This work aims to propose a high-order fully actuated system (FAS) model for discrete-time strict-feedback systems with nonuniform dimensions. In most of existing works, the authors only consider strict-feedback systems with uniform dimension, i.e., all subsystems have the same dimension. In contrast, we assume that the subsystems may have different or nonidentical dimensions. In particular, the dimensions are assumed to be increasing. Both step-forward and step-backward FAS models for discrete-time strict-feedback systems with nonuniform dimensions are given, based on which the exponentially stabilized controllers can be directly obtained.

articleTitle: Controllability of linear discrete periodic systems based on fully-actuated system approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Since linear discrete-periodic time-varying systems play an important role in both theory and practice, they have become the focus of research efforts in the field of control. The problem of controllability in the structural properties of linear discrete-periodic systems is considered in this paper, and a controllability criterion based on high-order fully-actuated system approaches is proposed. High-order fully-actuated models for linear discrete-periodic time-varying systems are constructed by this approach, and a sufficient and necessary condition is provided that the controllable linear discrete-periodic system can be equivalently transformed into a step-forward high-order fully-actuated model and a step-backward high-order fully-actuated model. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the validity and feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Finite-time Control for Nonlinear Systems with Full-state Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper considers the problem of finite-time tracking control for a class of nonlinear systems with asymmetric full-state constraints. To deal with the asymmetric full-state constraints, a nonlinear state-constrained function is constructed. A new finite-time tracking control strategy is proposed by using the designed nonlinear state-constrained function and backstepping approach. Meanwhile, to cope with the explosion of complexity problem of the traditional backstepping approach, the dynamic surface control method with first-order filter is introduced. The new design controller can not only ensure the finite-time convergent property of the all signals in the resulting system and tracking error, but also guarantee each state is constrained in the predefined region. Finally, the effectiveness of the obtained results is shown by illustrative example.

articleTitle: Parametric Approach to Missile Formation Control
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Under the condition of strong connectivity, the formation keeping problem of missile formation based on high-order fully actuated system is studied. The time-varying controller of the system is designed for the formation tracking of missile formation and disturbance suppression by upgrading the first-order model to the second-order model and using the parametric approach. The numerical simulation experiments of the system are completed with the introduction of bounded random disturbances. The motion trajectory, position tracking error, velocity tracking error and control force output of the missile formation are analyzed, and the final steady-state error is basically stabilized within 0.1, and the control force is controlled at about 2000 N during the formation holding phase.

articleTitle: H∞ admissibilization for second-order fully actuated fuzzy delayed singular impulsive systems with Markovian jump characteristic
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper researches H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> admissibilization for second-order fully actuated fuzzy delayed singular impulsive systems with Markovian jump characteristic. The second-order fully actuated single-link robot arm is successfully modeled as second-order fully actuated fuzzy delayed singular impulsive jump system by T-S fuzzy technique. The timer-dependent (T-R) L-K functional (L-KF) is constructed, which can better acquire the mixed information of Markovian modes and impulses. Meanwhile, the influence of the internal impulses is eliminated by singular value decomposition (SVD) technology. Improved sufficient conditions about stochastic admissibilization for second-order fully actuated fuzzy delayed singular impulsive jump systems are obtained in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) via fuzzy state-feedback controller (FSFC). Finally, the simulation example proves the validity and correctness of the result in this paper.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control for an Over-Actuated Vehicle on SO(3)
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Compared with the under-actuated unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) represented by the quadrotors, the over-actuated vehicles are more susceptible to modeling errors and external disturbances. In order to improve the ability of the over-actuated vehicles to resist internal and external disturbances, an attitude control approach based on SO(3) is proposed. By fully combining the nonlinear characteristics of geometry control on SO(3) and the anti-disturbance capability of the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), without introducing additional modeling errors, ADRC is extended to the attitude control of the vehicle. Meanwhile, the attitude controller is designed as a cascaded PID controller, which makes ADRC easy to be implemented. Due to the properties of the over-actuated vehicles, it is possible to achieve decoupled control of position and attitude, the position anti-disturbance control can be realized by directly applying ADRC. In our knowledge, this work is the first time that attitude ADRC is implemented on SO(3) for an over-actuated vehicle. Finally, through a series of comparative experiments, it is proved that, compared with traditional cascaded PID controllers, the attitude active disturbance rejection controller proposed in this paper can make the attitude control more stable and robust under wind disturbance, whether it is horizontal hovering or large-angle tilt hovering.

articleTitle: Bearing-only Circumnavigation Based on Fully Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of an agent with a second-order integrator dynamic model circumnavigating a static target in a circle orbit with desired distance and speed using bearing-only measurements. In this bearing-only problem, the agent only has access to its own motion information and the relative direction measurements of the target. Existing works only consider the first-order integrator dynamic model. In this paper, we apply the fully actuated system (FAS) approach to design a high-order controller and give a rigorous proof for the convergence of the closed-loop circumnavigation control system. A simulation is performed to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based High-Order Sliding Mode Control via High-Order Fully Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A RBF network based high-order sliding mode control (SMC) via high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approaches is studied in this paper. Firstly, a high-order sliding surface based on HOFA system approaches is proposed such that the sliding mode dynamics is obtained. By using radial basis function (RBF) neural network, the unknown function can be approximated. Then, the adaptive RBF sliding mode controller is designed for HOFA systems with the unknown parameters and uncertain nonlinearity vectors such that global asymptotical stability is ensured. Compared with the existing HOFA systems approaches, the proposed method can be applied to deal with the unknown continuous function. Finally, an example shows the validity of proposed methods.

articleTitle: Improved Flux Observer Based on Voltage-Current Hybrid Model for PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The accurate observation of the stator flux linkage directly affects the stability of PMSM torque closed-loop control. Aiming at the problems of integral saturation and DC bias existing in traditional flux observers, a flux observer based on a voltage-current hybrid model is proposed after theoretical analysis of the stator flux observer. The proposed flux observer combines the improved voltage model flux observer, which serially connects a low-pass filter (LPF) to a high-pass filter (HPF), with a current model flux observer, through a PI loop and phase compensation. The experimental results show that the improved hybrid model flux observer can achieve high observation accuracy and dynamic response to stator flux and electromagnetic torque, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of permanent-magnet eddy-current coupler speed control system based on fully-actuated system model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This note investigates the control design problem of a permanent-magnet eddy-current coupler (PEC) speed control system. To address this, the PEC speed control system is modeled as a fully-actuated system through electrical and kinematic equations. Considering the situation that the system state quantities are not directly accessible, an observer-based controller is developed using the separate design of the observer and state feedback. Meanwhile, a parametric method is adopted to calculate the gain matrix that allows the closed-loop control system to ensure stability while converging at a desired speed. Finally, the obtained results are effectively applied in a PEC speed control system example.

articleTitle: Fully Actuated System Game-Based Attitude Control for Combined Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, using the multiple microspacecrafts to carry out attitude takeover stabilization control for the failed spacecraft is studied in the sense of fully actuated system game-based method. According to the attitude dynamics, the fully-actuated system model of the combined spacecraft is established. And the game-based controller of the fully actuated system is designed for the combined spacecraft attitude control. Finally, numerical simulation indicates the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A Swarm Flocking Control Method of Spacecraft Cluster Flight
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Most conventional cooperative control methods are based on the top–down mechanisms. These mechanisms are usually centralized. In order to improve the viability of spacecraft cluster, a novel distributed flocking control combining the exponential function and the piecewise function is proposed to organize and guide spacecraft monomers to achieve the coordinated flocking behavior and the stable orbit operation. In addition, the spacecrafts can achieve the stable space to avoid collision. As the relative motion dynamics model of spacecraft is considered in the design of the flocking local rules, the proposed flocking model is practical in theory. Finally, a numerical simulation is carried out, which verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed flocking model.

articleTitle: Aircraft Attitude Control on High-order Fully Actuated System Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a second-order fully actuated system model is derived for a six degree of freedom aircraft model with control coupling. Then a three channel joint optimal attitude control method of roll, yaw and pitch is designed on high-order fully actuated system theory. Through mathematical simulation of this controller and the traditional PID controller, it is shown that the PID control method has a great shortage in the aircraft with control coupling, and the fully actuated system theory control method can well solve the problem of aircraft coupling, achieve the stable tracking of aircraft attitude command, and has better rapidity.

articleTitle: Compound Faults Parameter Estimation and Fault-tolerant Control in F-16 Fighter Flight Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Aims at the compound faults of the flight control system of F-16 fighter, which is composed of pitch rate sensor and aileron fault, this paper proposes a dual-channel state estimation scheme to estimate multiple fault parameters based on the observer principle at the same time. According to the fault estimation results, the flight control system can be fault-toleranted. The three-channel state coupling characteristic of pitch and yaw roll makes the control system introduce other fault information when detecting and diagnosing a single fault, which seriously reduces the accuracy of fault diagnosis. In this paper, by constructing two observers in different channels and designing the estimated parameter change rate in the observer based on Lyapunov stability theory, the residual error of the two observers can converge synchronously. Then the fault parameters can be estimated in the observer system. Based on the nonlinear dynamic inverse control scheme and the compensated state quantity, the flight control performance of the fighter can be improved.

articleTitle: A High-Order Fully Actuated Predictive Control Approach for Spacecraft Flying-Around
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This research investigates a spacecraft flying-around problem in a sight coordinate system. In this coordinate system, a nonlinear high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system model is adopted to establish the relative dynamics of spacecraft, such that the presented flying-around mission can be transformed into a tracking control problem of nonlinear HOFA systems. A HOFA predictive control approach is correspondingly proposed to implement this flying-around task. In this approach, the nonlinearities can be eliminated to construct a linear HOFA system because of full actuation characteristic, and then a linear incremental HOFA (LIHOFA) prediction model is constructed by applying a Diophantine equation to replace a reduced-order prediction model, such that the multi-step ahead predictions are developed to optimize the tracking control performance, which guarantees the realization of this flying-around mission. Further, two simulated examples of spacecraft flying-around are provided to verify the feasibility of HOFA predictive control approach.

articleTitle: Fully actuated system modeling and control of LCL grid-connected inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The LCL filter is widely used in new energy grid-connected systems because of its good high-frequency filtering characteristics, but it is a third-order system, and the design of the controller is relatively complicated. By using the inherent fully actuated characteristics of the system, the mathematical model of the system can be transformed into a fully actuated model, which can greatly simplify the design of the controller. In this paper, the fully actuated mathematical model of the LCL grid-connected inverter is established, and its control strategy is derived. At last, the stability of the control strategy is verified by the simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Fusion Framework Based on GPS State Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a GPS Fusion Framework Based on Graph optimization is proposed. Integrating visual inertial navigation odometer, a robust and high-precision UAV positioning algorithm for indoor and outdoor complex environments is completed. By using the proposed method, UAV platform can accurately obtain its own pose in indoor and outdoor, tunnel and other different environments. Compared with the pure visual positioning algorithm, the proposed multi-sensor fusion algorithm based on GPS state detection improves the positioning accuracy significantly. Finally, the algorithm is verified on the KITTI dataset and the quadrotor UAV platform. It is proven that the proposed algorithm has high precision and strong robustness.

articleTitle: Fully-actuated-system-approach-based Attitude-orbit Integrated Control for Spacecraft Formation Flying
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, an attitude-orbit integrated control law based on the fully-actuated system approach is proposed for spacecraft formation flying system. A 6DOF attitude-orbit integrated kinematic and dynamic model based on SE(3) description is established, and the fully-actuated system model is derived. Considering the effects of disturbances and unknown items of model, an adaptive neural network is designed to compensate the effects. Further, a fully-actuated-system-approach-based controller is developed for spacecraft formation flying tasks. The convergency of formation tracking error is proved via the Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, numerical results indicate the effectiveness of the control law proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Tracking Control for High-order Fully Actuated System with Input Constraints by Explicit Reference Governor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studies the tracking control problem of high-order fully actuated system subject to input constraints. Since there exist input constraints, an inappropriate reference signal being tracked may cause actuator saturation and further cause system instability. For solving the problem, we firstly design a generalized proportional differential controller to ensure the stability of the closed-loop system without input constraints. Then, an explicit reference governor is constructed to modify the reference signal such that the applied reference signal never exceeds the saturation limits, and the equilibrium of the resulting closed-loop system is globally asymptotically stable. Furthermore, we prove that the applied reference will converge to the original reference as much as possible. Therefore, the system output finally converges to the original reference by tracking the applied reference. A numerical example demonstrates the validity of the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: The fuzzy sliding mode control-based autonomous vehicle controller design
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Fuzzy control and sliding mode control technologies play an increasingly important role in a myriad of applications, like the autonomous vehicle systems. In this paper, the fuzzy model for the autonomous vehicle system with a dynamic positioning system is established firstly. Then the stability analysis and controller synthesis are provided, the solution method of the sliding mode control gain is synthesized. Finally, a simulation example provides evidence of the availability of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Resilient H∞ Observer Design for T-S Fuzzy System: A Flexible Edge Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the resilient $H_{\infty}$ observer design problem for T-S fuzzy system is considered by flexible edge structure, whose the flexible edge structure mainly embody that the desired observer could bear definite perturbances on its parameter matrices. Different from the current observer design methods, the flexible edge can be calculated, and the calculated edge gain can explicitly characterize the tolerance measure of the resilient observer. A sufficient condition ensuring asymptotic stability and $H_{\infty}$ performance of the observer error system is established by a double variables-based decoupling principle, and the flexible edge and the observer gains can be both achieved. The effectiveness of the proposed design approach is illustrated by two examples.

articleTitle: Automatic Intermittent Humidification Control Systems based on Grey Box Models
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: As living standards are improving, people have higher requirements for comfort and health in their living environment. Indoor temperature and humidity are two important factors that affect human comfort. Previous research has mainly focused on indoor temperature environment, while research on humidity environment is relatively simple, usually only considering energy consumption and humidity stability issues. Therefore, traditional humidity control methods can no longer meet the needs of intermittent use of houses. This article establishes gray box models of humidification room systems and estimates the time required for advance humidification based on the models. Subsequently, a fully automatic intermittent humidification control system is designed using MATLAB and STM32, which achieved functions such as user interaction interface, data automatic acquisition, model automatic identification, and algorithm automatic execution. Finally, the effectiveness and universality of the fully automatic intermittent humidification control system are verified through experiments.

articleTitle: A fault diagnosis algorithm of the dedicated equipment based on CBAM-ResNET mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: With the increase of the intellectualization of the dedicated equipment, the coupling degree between different electronic devices is also increasing, and the signals contained in the dedicated equipment are also growing. Therefore, it is difficult to use statistical methods for fault diagnosis, but now the fault diagnosis of equipments mainly adopts machine learning for small samples or deep learning. This paper proposes a neural network model based on convolutional block attention module (CBAM)-Residual neural network (ResNET) for fault diagnosis of the dedicated equipment. First, the data is preprocessed according to the mechanism of the equipment. Then, the jump connection of the residual neural network is used to alleviate the problem of gradient disappearance and information loss. The CBAM mechanism is used to combine the channel attention mechanism (CAM) and spatial attention mechanism (SAM), which can better reflect the characteristics of the data. In this paper, an experimental simulation platform is designed, which is used to obtain the fault data and verify the fault model. The fault model proposed in this paper is compared with the traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The results show that this model has higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Transformer Based Multi-model Fusion for 3D Facial Animation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The topic of 3D drivable facial animation has been extensively studied for many years. Due to the limited audiovisual data and the uncertainty of the problem, it is still challenging to generate faithful facial motions. Most existing research focuses mainly on using audio information, which easily leads to excessively smooth lip movements during the generation. Considering the progress of multimodal learning and the advantages of phoneme-based mapping-driven approaches. We combine the phoneme and text representation into the task to enhance the relationship between speech and animation. Specifically, we present a novel multi-model fusion Transformer for the 3D facial generation that learns the features from audio, text, and phonemes modality. Utilizing the intrinsic relationship between phonemes and corresponding mouth movements can constrain excessive smoothness in the mapping from audio to mouth movements. Using powerful language representation models to obtain contextual semantic information from the text can eliminate facial animation biases caused by individual speaking characteristics in the audio. Additionally, to explore the rich information between modalities, we also introduce an attention-based fusion mechanism to integrate related features. The qualitative and quantitative experiments proved our method’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Intelligent medical image reconstruction: PET image denoising and super-resolution joint processing based on generating adversarial network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: PET (Positron Emission Tomography) is one of the advanced imaging technologies in nuclear medicine. It is now widely used in diagnosing many diseases, determining conditions, evaluating efficacy, performing organ function research, and developing new drugs. However, due to the characteristics of nuclear medicine technology, PET is still a low-count and low- resolution imaging method. Therefore, solving the high noise and low resolution of PET images is essential. This paper proposes a multitask least square generative Adversarial Network (MultiLSGAN) for joint noise-reduction-super-resolution reconstruction of low-quality PET images. This paper proposes a Multitask Least Square Generative Adversarial Network (MultiLSGAN) for joint noise-reduction-super-resolution reconstruction of low-quality PET images. The method is targeted for noise-reduction- super-resolution imaging tasks with supervised learning. Based on the loss function of the original GAN, we introduce the VGG model to calculate the perceptual loss and add mean square error (MSE), gradient, total variance, and other loss function constraints to generate images. Finally, experiments are conducted using the data provided by Neusoft Medical, and the quantitative and qualitative results of MultiLSGAN are better compared with the advanced methods.

articleTitle: Attitude Tracking Control of Launcher with Structural Misalignment Based on Fully-Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper tackles the attitude tracking control problem of a launcher subject to structural uncertainty during orbit injection. By doing so, a nonlinear attitude dynamics is firstly formulated. The system uncertainties mainly caused by structural uncertainty is considered and then handled by introducing Neumann Series. Afterwards, a nonlinear control scheme is proposed, composed of a feedforward compensator and feedback controller. The feedback gain matrices are designed by fully-actuated system approach to ensure a comprehensively satisfactory performance. At last, numerical simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Unmanned Surface Vehicle with Unknown Nonlinearity and Actuator Degradation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper develops a fault tolerant control method for unmanned surface vehicle with unknown nonlinearity, actuator degradation and external disturbance simultaneously. The sliding mode controller is designed first to eliminate the effects of disturbances, where the quantization errors between the unmanned surface vehicle and the remote control station can be compensated. Then, the adaptive mechanism updated online is applied to deal with the unknown nonlinearity and actuator degradation. Furthermore, the proposed control law is shown to guarantee the strict stability and reachability of the sliding surface. Finally, the feasibility of this method is verified by conducting experimental simulation.

articleTitle: Partial-Nodes-Based State Estimation for Complex Networks with Buffer Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This article focuses on the ultimate boundedness estimation problem for a class of partial-node-based (PNB) complex networks (CNs) with buffer constraint. The aim of the addressed estimation problem is designing an estimator for the PNB complex network so that the estimation error system is ultimately bounded. Sufficient conditions are obtained to ensure the ultimate boundedness of the dynamics of the estimation error system. Furthermore, the ideal estimator gain is derived through solving a convex optimization problem. Finally, an illustrative example is provided to illustrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed estimator designing approach.

articleTitle: Assessment of Network Security Situation of Industrial Control System Based on CG-ELM
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a network security situation assessment model of the industrial control system, and the model divides the industrial control network security situation assessment into two subtasks: threat traffic detection and determination of hierarchical weight. The purpose of threat traffic detection is to detect possible network attacks in network data traffic. In order to identify network attacks quickly and accurately, this paper uses the extreme learning machine model to classify network attacks, and uses the conjugate gradient method to improve the training efficiency of the extreme learning machine model. For the purpose of assessing the impact of different network attacks on the security situation of industrial control systems, this paper proposes a hierarchical industrial control network model for situation assessment based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process. The experimental verification of the situation assessment is carried out on the simulation platform of the sewage treatment industrial control system.

articleTitle: A Longitudinal Fuzzy Variable Parameter Model Based on Sector Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: We study a longitudinal fuzzy variable parameter model of Mars probe using sector nonlinearity. Compared with the traditional longitudinal dynamic model, we overcome the shortcoming of the sharp increase in the number of fuzzy rules when the traditional T-S fuzzy model describes time-varying system and reduce the complexity of the model by means of linearization. Then we design a full state feedback and a dynamical output feedback gain-scheduling controllers based on the quadratic Lyapunov stability theorem for the Mars probe’s entry phase. Finally, the simulation results from Matlab are used to demonstrate the superiority of the model.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Sliding-Mode Control for Consensus of Second-Order Leader-Following Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the consensus problem of second-order leader-following multi-agent systems based on event-triggered sliding-mode control. Firstly, the sliding mode surface is designed to ensure that the states of the multi-agent system asymptotically converge on the surface. Subsequently, an event-triggered protocol is proposed to reduce the energy consumption of multi-agent systems. The protocol enables the multi-agent system to reach the sliding mode surface in finite time and achieve consensus. In addition, the occurrence of Zeno behavior is ruled out. Finally, simulations are conducted to verify the main results of this paper.

articleTitle: Fractional Gradient Descent Method for Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A fractional-order gradient descent method applicable to spiking neural networks(SNNs) is proposed for the problem of difficulty in training SNNs using stochastic gradient descent method. The method is an improvement of the location of the gradient backpropagation calculation in the training of SNNs and the output form of the last layer in the structure, respectively, and the convergence is proved using the fractional-order difference expression under the Grünwald-Letnikov definition. The test results on both pure SNN and CNN2SNN models simultaneously show that the method can effectively reduce the number of sample cycle inputs and thus the training time without reducing the accuracy.

articleTitle: Guaranteed cost attitude control of spacecraft under control limitation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the guaranteed cost attitude control problem of spacecrafts under parameter uncertainty and control limitation is studied, the tradeoff relationship between system performance and control input is discussed, and a new guaranteed cost attitude control method is proposed independent on model linearization technology. This method takes into account the inherent nonlinear characteristics of spacecraft attitude systems. By exploring the characteristics of attitude dynamics described by quaternion and using special analysis techniques, the asymptotic stability is ensured, based on which the constraint relationship between performance index and control torque limits is established. Through the constraint, a linear controller can be determined that meets simultaneously the predetermined performance index and control torque limits. Moreover, the allowable optimal system performance can be obtained under some given maximal control torque limit, and the required minimal control torque can be analyzed under a prescribed performance index. Finally, the results of numerical experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and its advantages compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: Design of Dynamic Output Feedback Controller for Positive T-S Fuzzy Systems Based on Event-Triggered Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a study is conducted on the dynamic output feedback controller design of positive Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems under the context of the event-triggered mechanism. Firstly, the conditions for the event-triggered dynamic output feedback controller of positive T-S fuzzy systems are adopted, which can ensure the positivity and stability of the closed-loop system. Then, it is proved that there is the Zeno-free phenomenon in the system. Finally, the validity of the calculated results is verified by the injurious insect population model.

articleTitle: Stabilization for discrete-time Markovian jumping LPV systems with cyber attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The stabilization problem is studied for discrete-time Markovian jumping linear parameter varying (LPV) systems with cyber attacks. Considering that there exist some difficulties in obtaining all transition probability for practical systems, the discrete-time Markovian model with partially unknown transition probabilities is introduced. Sufficient criterion for mean-square stability is obtained by means of Lyapunov function theory. Then, under the framework of random DoS attacks, the corresponding feedback controller is constructed to realize the mean-square stability of the underlying system. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by simulating the turbofan engine model.

articleTitle: Switching control for a class of sub-fully actuated systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studied stability of a class of sub-fully actuated systems under the framework of high-order fully-actuated system approach. The under-actuated set is described by a hyperplane. A switching control law is designed for the sub-fully actuated system, where the control input equals to zero when the state trajectory is in the neighborhood of the under-actuated set; and the control input is designed the same as fully-actuated case otherwise. Under certain conditions, the state trajectory of the closed-loop system will cross the under-actuated hyperplane and converge to the origin exponentially.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Optimal Design of Disk Permanent Magnet Eddy Current Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the analytical modeling and optimization of disk permanent magnet eddy-current couplers are studied. A fairly accurate steady-state model considering the complete leakage magnetic circuit is established using the equivalent magnetic circuit method, which is capable of considering geometric parameters and material properties. Then, the optimal structural parameters of the selected coupler are obtained by the Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) algorithm. Finally, the calculation results are verified by finite element analysis and experimental experiments.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Attitude Tracking Control of Spacecraft Formation with Prescribed Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper is developed for attitude tracking control of spacecraft formation to reduce the communication burden. Based on the backstepping technology and prescribed performance function, a new adaptive distributed event-triggered control law is proposed which possesses the following properties: 1) The communication burden of formation is reduced for only the attitude information of the neighbors is required to be exchanged. 2) The communication burden is further reduced by employing a event-triggered mechanism, which only sends the sampling states at the event-triggering instants to the control module. 3) Attitude tracking errors can converge to predefined arbitrarily small residual sets. Finally, A simulation example is employed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Tracking Design for Uncertain Time-Delay Systems with Pure-Feedback Terms
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the tracking design issue for the nonlinear time-delay switched systems (NTDSSs) with unknown pure-feedback terms. The pure-feedback terms can be indifferentiable and the controllability of each subsystem is not required. We use the neural networks approach to approximate these unknown feedback terms, and a stabilizing switching law is co-designed to construct a controller, under which the trajectory of the closed-loop NTDSSs are bounded, and the tracking problem is addressed. Finally, we give an example to verifies the methods.

articleTitle: Consensus control of linear multi-agent systems based on state observer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The paper considers observer-based consensus problem for both continuous-time and discrete-time linear multi-agent systems over undirected networks. It is assumed that the agent have knowledge of its own full state and can observe its neighbors’ state. By designing state observer, the neighbors’ state is estimated. The distributed consensus protocol is designed by applying the error of the agent’s own full state and the neighbors’ estimated state. By means of separation principle, it is proved that the multi-agent systems can reach consensus under the proposed consensus protocol. Finally, the validity of the results is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Optimal Fault Estimation and Fault-tolerant Control for Spacecraft Formation via Stackelberg Differential Game approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this work, a deep investigation has been conducted into the optimal fault estimation and accommodation problem for spacecraft formation flying, which has resulted in the formulation of a fault-tolerant formation control scheme using the framework of Stackelberg differential game theory. Within the framework of the Stackelberg game, the role of the leader is assumed by the fault observer, while the leader is impersonated by the spacecraft formation system, thereby establishing sequential decisions between the follower and the leader. To achieve the Stackelberg equilibrium, an auxiliary controller is designed for the follower, enabling a non-cooperative game with the control strategy of the leader. To facilitate the online updating of the schemes of the follower and the leader, the reinforcement learning control scheme is applied, utilizing two Actor-Cntic neural networks for the observer and spacecraft formation system, respectively. Ultimately, the simulation is carried out to achieve the optimal fault estimation and accommodation targets, thereby illustrating the efficiency and applicability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Resilient Fault-Tolerant State Estimation for Systems over Sensor Networks with Intermittent Faults under Weighted Try-Once-Discard Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The problem of resilient state estimation with intermittent faults is studied for the discrete system over sensor networks under the Weighted Try-Once-Discard (WTOD) protocol in this paper. A fault estimator is established to estimate intermittent faults, so as to ensure that the state estimator can maintain performance regardless of whether the system has intermittent fault. The WTOD protocol is used for deciding information transmission between nodes. Moreover, the resilient estimator was devised to restrain the detrimental influence caused by imprecise estimator parameters. Through the recursive linear matrix inequality technique, the $H_{\infty}$ performance constraints in a finite-honzon is warranted. Eventually, the practicability and validity of the suggested approach is demonstrated through a numerical example.

articleTitle: Output Feedback-Based Refined Fault-Tolerant Control for Drag-Free Satellites with Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, an output feedback-based refined fault-tolerant control strategy for drag-free satellites is investigated to counteract actuator fault and disturbance. The coupling of disturbance and fault in the same channel will affect the reliability of fault diagnosis and the control precision of drag-free satellites. Therefore, an observer-based method is designed to realize the fault diagnosis by the separation estimation of disturbance and fault, even though the relative velocity information is not measurable. More specifically, according to the modellable characteristics of disturbance and the non-modellable characteristics of actuator fault, a reduced-order state observer (ROSO) is designed to estimate the disturbance and the relative velocity information, and an extended state observer (ESO) is designed to estimate the actuator fault. Then, by incorporating a sliding mode controller, a composite control law is proposed to enhance the anti-disturbance and fault-tolerant capability of satellites. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Formation tracking for the heterogeneous multi-agents under deception attacks: an impulsive control approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the formation tracking problem for heterogeneous multi-agent systems subject to deception attacks. Due to the openness of communication networks, false data, usually generated by deception attacks, can be injected into communication channels and thereby destroy the integrity and correctness of transmitted data. To deal with such threats, this paper proposes a novel distributed time-varying formation tracking control protocol based on impulse control. By designing an impulse-based compensator, the attacked information transmitted from leader to follower can be estimated precisely. And therefore, a new resilient tracking impulse controller is constructed based on the information of state feedback, estimated leader, and formation shape. Then, explicit criteria are derived for the gains of the desired compensator and controllers, under which the mean square exponential uniformly roundness is ensured for the tracking error dynamics. Moreover, the adopted impulse-based strategy can greatly reduce the information interaction and improve the communicating reliability of the heterogeneous multi-agents. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed formation controller is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Distributed Flocking Control of Aerial Vehicles Based on a Markov Random Field
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The distributed flocking control of collective aerial vehicles has extraordinary advantages in scalability and reliability, etc. However, it is still challenging to design a reliable, efficient, and responsive flocking algorithm. In this paper, a distributed predictive flocking framework is presented based on a Markov random field (MRF). The MRF is used to characterize the optimization problem that is eventually resolved by discretizing the input space. Potential functions are employed to describe the interactions between aerial vehicles and as indicators of flight performance. The dynamic constraints are taken into account in the candidate feasible trajectories which correspond to random variables. Numerical simulation shows that compared with some existing latest methods, the proposed algonthm has better-flocking cohesion and control efficiency performances. Experiments are also conducted to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: The Structure-preserving Doubling Algorithm for the Discrete Coupled Riccati Matrix Equations
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the structure-preserving doubling algorithm (SDA) is considered to solve a discrete coupled Riccati matrix equation (DCRME) arising in Markov Jump Systems. Firstly, we transform the DCRME into a standard symplectic form using methods developed for symmetric structures. With the symplectic form, the SDA is established to obtain a positive definite solution to the DCRME. It is demonstrated that the matrix sequences generated by the SDA converge quadratically. Finally, the numerical example is provided to illustrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the presented SDA.

articleTitle: SSRL: A Safe and Smooth Reinforcement Learning Approach for Collision Avoidance in Navigation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the collision avoidance problem of autonomous robots using reinforcement learning (RL) techniques, with a focus on ensuring both safety and smoothness. To achieve stability guarantees, a data-based Lyapunov function is incorporated into the model-free RL framework for training policies. Furthermore, constraints on action increments and action distributions are introduced, which effectively mitigate the differences between adjacent actions and ensuring smoothness in the learned policies. Subsequently, a safe and smooth reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed for training navigation policies, and its superiority in terms of safety and smoothness are validated by using a ground mobile robot in a simulated environment.

articleTitle: Elevator Fault Prediction and Early Warning Method Based on ERNIE Pre-training
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In view of the practical needs of 96333 elevator emergency disposal, based on the 59,789 answering and handling records of 96333 elevator emergency disposal service platform from 2017 to now, the elevator fault cause analysis and fault type classification were carried out by integrating expert experience to form standardized marked data. On this basis, the ERNIE(Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration) Tiny pre-training model is applied for migration learning to realize automatic classification of access hotline fault types and causes and auxiliary reminder. The practical application shows that artificial intelligence technology can play a positive role in improving the effectiveness of elevator emergency service and has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Distribution consensus of multi-agent systems based on model predictive control with probability density function
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A distributed output feedback model predictive control approach based on the probability density function method is proposed to realize multi-agent distribution consensus. Each agent solves the optimal control input by estimating the worst-case local error and perturbation, modeled into a local min-max optimization problem. In the iterative solving process, the agent i will send its information to its neighbor agent through the communication topology, so as to achieve the convergence of group consensus error. Under the assumption of controllability and observability, the proposed control method provides an upper bound for the group distribution consensus error, thus ensuring the practical distribution consensus performance under unmeasured interference and noise.

articleTitle: Multi-target tracking control system of phased array antenna with mechanical scanning and beam scanning method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In the field of telemetry, track, and command system, this study presents a phased array antenna control system for achieving multi-target tracking tasks through a set of systems. Firstly, electric beam scanning of a planar array phased array antenna is used in this paper to implement multi-target tracking. In addition, the phased array antenna is mounted on the antenna pedestal, which can operate on the azimuth and elevation mechanical axes. Thirdly, the mechanical scanning method of the azimuth-elevation antenna pedestal and the beam scanning method of the phased array antenna are combined to realize multi-target tracking tasks. Finally, the experiments of flight tracking are completed by employing the technique of UAV tagging, and the results validate the viability of the system.

articleTitle: GPS-free Stabilization Control for Autonomous Vehicle without Parking Space Marking: Simulation and Experiment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the stabilization control problem for autonomous vehicles in GPS-denied environments, specifically addressing the challenge of automatic parking without access to parking space marking information. The geometric planning approach is proposed to find alternative reference points for vehicles in the absence of parking space markings. Subsequently, the proposed geometric planning combined with relative pose measurement, is utilized to develop automatic parking control laws for scenarios without parking space marking information. These control laws ensure safe navigation and enable automatic parking in both obstacle-free and obstacle-blocked scenarios. Eventually, the effectiveness and performance of the proposed controllers are validated through numerical simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Disturbance Rejection Based Predictive Control of Discrete-Time Networked Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the control problem of networked control systems (NCSs) with time delays and mismatched disturbances in the discrete-time domain. A novel composite controller which is composed of networked predictive unit and disturbance rejection unit, is proposed for the considered NCSs. To be specific, an observer-based networked predictive unit is responsible for an active compensation of time delays, while a disturbance rejection unit is constructed to deal with the mismatched disturbances effectively. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control method is demonstrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based MPC for Tracking Control of 4WID4WIS
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: To achieve trajectory tracking with 4wiswid(Four wheel independent drive and Four wheel-independent steering), a reinforcement learning-based linear model predictive control(MPC) controller is designed. The controller is designed based on the kinematics model of 4WID4WIS, but the dynamics are unknown. Adding reinforcement learning to learn errors caused by unknown dynamics, adjust the weight matrix to reduce the error, and improve the control performance of the system. The stability of the proposed reinforcement learning-based MPC has been demonstrated by Lyapunov. The proposed control method has a fast response speed and good robustness. Simulation and experiments are given to demonstrate the availability of this method.

articleTitle: Dynamic Observer and Disturbance Observer Based Fault Estimation and Fault-Tolerant Control of Switched Fuzzy Stochastic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, fault estimation and fault-tolerant control of switched fuzzy systems with fault, disturbance and stochastic noise are studied. Considering the presence of actuator fault in this system. When the fault size changes frequently, the classical proportional-integral observer is not easy to obtain accurate estimation results. Therefore, we design a dynamic observer, and introduce the derivative of output feedback to improve the estimation performance. At the same time, the disturbance observer is added, which can simultaneously estimate the system state, actuator fault and disturbance. Based on the estimated information, a fault-tolerant controller is constructed. Finally, the linear matrix inequality conditions have been obtained, which make the whole system is mean-square exponentially stable with root-mean-square performance.

articleTitle: Spacecraft Attitude Control with Fully Actuated System and Particle Swarm Optimization Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, attitude tracking control of spacecraft is studied. Firstly, the fully actuated system models of rigid body satellite is established, and then the linear sliding mode controller is designed by direct parameterization method. One of the key problems in direct parameterization is the tuning of matrix parameters. Aiming at the difficulty of parameter setting of spacecraft attitude controller based on fully actuated system approach, a parameter setting method based on particle swarm optimization algorithm was proposed. Particle swarm optimization is used to adjust matrix parameters more quickly and accurately. At the same time, inertia weight factor is introduced to avoid the early local optimal phenomenon of particle swarm optimization algorithm. Simulation results reveal the effect of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: Maximum correntropy Kalman filter algorithm with two-step random delay and packet loss
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Due to the limited width of the communication channel, data delay and packet loss occur at the receiver when receiving measurement data. The number of delay steps is random, but the probability of delay occurrence decreases as the number of steps increases. Therefore, in this paper, we use a binary Bernoulli distribution to model measurement data with known delay probability, and redesign the Kalman filter(KF) and Maximum correntropy Kalman filter (MCKF) algorithms to accommodate a system with two steps of random delay and packet loss. We compare the improved KF and MCKF algorithms under Gaussian noise and non-Gaussian noise systems, and the experimental results show that the improved KF and MCKF algorithms possess high estimation accuracy under Gaussian noise and non-Gaussian noise systems, respectively, when the systems undergoe two-step random delay and packet loss.

articleTitle: Discrete feedback stabilization of highly nonlinear neutral stochastic Markovian jump systems with multiple delays
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper explores the discrete feedback stabilization of highly nonlinear neutral stochastic Markovian jump systems (HNNSMJSs). Different from the existing literature, the neutral terms of these HNNSMJSs contain multiple delays and Markovian jump parameters. Firstly, the existence, uniqueness and boundedness of the solution are proved under some reasonable conditions. Secondly, a feedback control based on the discrete-time state observations is designed to stabilize an unstable HNNSMJS. Then, by applying the method of Lyapunov functional, the asymptotic stability of the controlled system is discussed. The upper bound of the time interval between two consecutive state observations is also given. Finally, a numerical example is provided to illustrate the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Global Output-Feedback Tracking Control for Uncertain Planar Nonlinear Systems with Polynomial Growth
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the adaptive tracking control problem for a class of nonlinear systems with unknown output polynomial growth. By combining ideas of universal control and deadzone with the backstepping technique, this paper proposes a new adaptive output-feedback tracking control scheme which incorporates an observer consisting of two dynamic high-gain update laws. The results show that the designed controller ensures that the tracking error converges to a prescribed arbitrarily small interval range after a finite time, while ensuring that the closed-loop system is globally bounded. Finally, the simulation example illustrates that the proposed tracking control scheme is effective.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment for Leader-following UAV Formation via Belief Rule Base
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The article puts focus on the the problem of performance assessment for UAV formation with leader-following structure and switching communication topology in the presence of unknown exogenous perturbations. First, two time-varying indicators are devised on the basis of the regulated outputs of the followers. Then, a trainable performance assessment model is constructed by means of belief rule base expert system (BRB) with the two time-varying indicators as the inputs and the assessment utility as the final output. At last, relevant simulation experiments are conducted to validate the practicability of the established performance assessment model for leader-following UAV formation subject to switching communication topology and unknown external perturbations.

articleTitle: Adaptive prescribed performance control for uncertain nonlinear HOFA systems with time delay
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the adaptive prescribed performance control problem for high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system with time delay. Different from the existing results, the proposed adaptive prescribed performance control method can ensure that the HOFA time-delay system can achieve semi-globally practical finite-time stable. In addition, the settling time of this paper is independent of design parameters and initial conditions. Hence, it can be set to any value. Finally, a practical example of a thermoacoustic unstable system in the Rijke tube is selected to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the scheme.

articleTitle: An Automatic Collision Avoidance with Disturbance Interval Observer for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: An automatic collision avoidance with disturbance interval observer (DIOB) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in non-cooperative uncertain environments is proposed in this paper. First, the collision detection condition and the linear time-varying collision avoidance model based on the collision cone are given. And, the anti-disturbance control law with DIOB is designed to ensure the safety of UAV collision avoidance. Then, the stability of the UAV collision avoidance control system with DIOB is proved through the Lyapunov theory. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve UAV automatic collision avoidance in unknown obstacle acceleration.

articleTitle: H∞ Consensus Design and Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems with Time-Varying Delay
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper takes multi-agent systems (MASs) under switching communication topologies as the research object, and studies the multi-agent systems consensus problem in view of communication delay in complex environment. Based on the average dwell time (ADT) method and Lyapunov function theory, sufficient conditions for the stability and robustness of the systems are given. The model uncertainty is estimated and compensated online in real time based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms, which improves the robustness of the system against strong uncertainties and disturbances while ensuring the stability. Through comparative simulations, it is proved that the optimized control system has better control accuracy and dynamic performance, which can enhance the reliability and intelligence of multi-flight formation.

articleTitle: Adaptive failure compensation tracking controller design for hypersonic vehicle based on high-order fully actuated system theory
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Hypersonic vehicle has great application potential and economic value both in military and civil use. The design of the controller is the key and core part of realising hypersonic technology.
