This paper designs the height and speed tracking controller of the longitudinal model of the hypersonic aircraft cruise stage based on the theory of the hypersonic vehicle in the dynamic model of the NASA Langley laboratory and using the theory of the high-order fully actuated system. At the same time, when the avehicle has double rudder surface redundancy, considering the size of the fault, mode and time unknown jammed failure on the rudder surface, the parameter adaptive law is introduced to complete the height fault tolerance tracking control of the aircraft to ensure that the system can realise fault self-compensation and improve the reliability of the controller. According to Lyapunov stability theorem, the stability of the system is proved. Finally, the simulation is used to further verify the theoretical rationality and feasibility, and the tracking curve shows that the designed controller has a good control effect.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Control Method for Non-minimum Phase Hypersonic Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive control method for hypersonic vehicle with non-minimum phase characteristics caused by the coupling of aerodynamic force and thrust. Firstly, for the velocity subsystem, the unknown uncertain aerodynamic parameters are estimated by adopting adaptive control method. Secondly, for the non-minimum phase flight path angle subsystem, it is decomposed into linear part and nonlinear part based on the assumption that dynamic pressure and velocity are constant. For the linear part, a model reference adaptive controller is designed; For the nonlinear part, the minimum norm control is used to eliminate the nonlinear term brought by the nonlinear part in the Lyapunov stability analysis, and the controller is improved to solve the singularity of the controller. Finally, the system stability of the proposed method is analyzed by using Lyapunov theory, and the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive controller is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Filtering Feature Selection Algorithm based on Fusion Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper mainly concerns filtering algorithms for feature selection of high-dimensional data in the field of machine learning. Feature selection implies that some of data is useless or even plays a negative role for machine learning, more specifically, there are redundant and invalid features among them. This paper applies fusion strategy for feature selection by combining different filtenng standards to obtain a new one. The basic architecture of step-by-step filtering is described in order to ensure the accuracy and efficiency of feature selection, upon which the Relief-F-MRMR filtering criterion and specific operation steps are designed. An illustrative example is provided to show the validity and advantage of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Microgrid operation optimization based on Wild Horse Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studies a microgrid system’s daily dispatching operation strategy under grid-connected mode based on Wild Horse Optimizer. Firstly, considering the grid-connected mode with the lowest power generation cost and the best environmental benefit, an optimization operation model of microgrids is established. Then, the wild horse optimization algorithm is used to implement the optimal scheduling of the model, and the algorithm’s superior performance is verified by comparing it with other algorithms. Finally, the simulation outcomes show that the wild horse optimization algorithm can effectively enhance microgrids’ economic and environmental benefits.

articleTitle: Multi-UAVs Formation Fault-Tolerant Control Based on the Adaptive Backstepping Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The open issue of fault-tolerant control for multi-UAVs formation is discussed in this study. A formation fault-tolerant control method based on the adaptive backstepping approach is developed to quickly form the original formation under actuator faults of the multi-UAVs. The formation is consisted of three UAVs to form a regular triangular formation and a virtual leader is embedded in the geometric center. The tracking error model of each UAV is created by applying the guiding technique. The communication connection among UAVs is determined based on the knowledge of graph theory. Fault parameters are estimated by the adaptive law based on discontinuous projection operator. The multi-UAVs formation fault-tolerant control law is obtained by combining with the backstepping approach. On the basis of the Lyapunov stability theory, the multi-UAVs formation fault-tolerant control system is stable. Finally, the results are shown that the UAVs can keep the required formation flight in the event of actuator faults.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control design of interconnected systems with time delay
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of dynamic integral sliding mode control of interconnected systems with time delay. Difference from the previous works, to fully adopt the characteristics of both the system state and control input, an interesting type of integral sliding surface is defined. It should be pointed out that the dynamic integral sliding mode control is designed to assure the system trajectories onto the predefined integral sliding surface despite disturbance. Linear matrix inequality is used to obtain the stability conditions to ensure sliding mode dynamics with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance.

articleTitle: Spacecraft Fault Warning Method Based on Adaptive Trend Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The on-orbit spacecraft monitoring system currently has a weak trend fault warning capacity that is typically relied on manually summarizing expert knowledge to identify abnormalities in advance. Furthermore, the expertise of the person in charge largely determines the breadth, depth, and accuracy of the knowledge. While the development of manually enhanced warning knowledge may also be hindered by the specific vanations of individual machines, various working modes, and environmental influencing elements. This work suggests an universal spacecraft fault warning method based on adaptive trend filtering in order to improve the automation of trend fault warning in the on-orbit spacecraft monitoring system while assuring the warning accuracy. Using the Ll trend filtering algonthm, a spacecraft fault warning model is created by fusing on-orbit telemetry data with knowledge of the mechanics of the spacecraft, expanding the fault samples to create a sample set for the improvement of the warning knowledge. On this basis, the simulated annealing algorithm is used to solve the key parameters in the spacecraft fault warning model, so as to quickly establish model for different spacecraft and provide strong support for the spacecraft on-orbit fault warning work.

articleTitle: Controllability, stability and design for high-order fully actuated systems: Special cases studies
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The high-order fully actuated (HOFA) model of a general dynamic control system makes it easy to design controllers, where HOFA model can make the closed-loop system become a constant linear system by a fully configurable characteristic structure. Based on this special property, the controllability of the general dynamic control system is discussed in the HOFA model. Then, the HOFA model under special cases: the low-order dynamic cases, are studied, which can generally be represented by a controllable subsystem and an additional uncontrollable subsystem or complementary subsystem. The general dynamic control system, if there is no uncontrollable subsystem, or it is stable in some sense, it is said to be stable. Finally, a typical tank system is take as an example to present that how to design the control low based on HOFA method. Simulations are carried out to illustrate the effectiveness of the control low design.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inversion-Based Adaptive Fault Tolerant Control for Heavy Launch Vehicles with Non-lethal Actuator Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes the dynamic inversion-based adaptive fault tolerant control for heavy launch vehicles with non-lethal actuator faults. Firstly, the attitude dynamics model and fault model of heavy launch vehicles are formulated. Secondly, based on the dynamic inversion theory, the ideal controller is designed. Then, the controller and adaptive law are designed for actuator gain faults and bias faults. Meanwhile, the Lyapunov function is constructed to prove that all signals in the closed-loop system are uniformly convergent. Finally, numerical simulation results show the effectiveness and the satisfactory performance of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Trajectory Control of Mars Probe Based on Fuzzy Lyapunov Function
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The trajectory control of the entry phase of the Mars probe plays a more and more important role in the whole pinpoint landing. Based on this background, this paper employs the sector nonlinearity to construct the longitudinal fuzzy dynamic model of the Mars probe’s entry phase. Different from the traditional quadratic Lyapunov function, the stability condition of the fuzzy parameter varying system based on the fuzzy Lyapunov function is proposed to reduce the conservatism of the system in this paper. Furthermore, the corresponding gain-scheduling controllers are designed to ensure asymptotic stability of the system. Numerical simulations are provided to intuitively demonstrate the effectiveness of the results.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inversion Control for Hypersonic Vehicle with Extended State Observer and PSO
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear control problem for hypersonic vehicle with uncertainties. The model of hypersonic vehicle is established. Considering the strong nonlinearity and strong coupling of hypersonic vehicle longitudinal model, the dynamic inversion is applied to decouple it. To overcome undesirable response caused by unmolded dynamics and external disturbances, the extended state observer is developed to estimate and compensate them. Meanwhile, the parameters of observer are optimized by using particle swarm optimization algorithm to improve the performance of controller. Numerical simulation is given to verify the effectiveness of proposed control method and PSO algorithm, where the unmolded dynamics and external disturbances is considered. The results of simulation show that the controller designed by proposed method have good tracking performance.

articleTitle: Integrated Design of Normal and Fault Modes for Spacecraft Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated design method of normal and fault modes for spacecraft control systems. The proposed method can not only achieve sub-optimal performance for the fault-free system but also retain the desired performance through system reconfiguration despite the occurrence of actuator faults, striking a good balance between the nominal performance in the normal mode and system reconfigurability in fault modes. First, a reliable controller is designed to keep the system robustly stable against actuator faults with a performance bound. Then, the conservativeness of the controller is further reduced to improve the nominal performance since a system is expected to run for the longest time in the nominal modes. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed method is verified via an example of the spacecraft attitude control system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Discrete Sliding-mode Predictive Control of Networked Multi-agent Control System Based on the Incremental Model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Sliding mode predictive control (SMPC) is a control method that combines sliding mode control (SMC) and mode predictive control (MPC). It has broad application prospects in networked multi-agent control system (NMACS) due to its strong robustness, good response speed, and anti-interference ability. Discrete sliding mode variable structure control based on discrete systems has the advantages of SMPC, but due to the influence of discrete reaching law and sampling period of discrete systems, the system control often exhibits chattering. To overcome the chattering problem of SMPC, this paper designs an adaptive discrete sliding mode predictive control (ADSMPC) scheme based on incremental models, and by designing a leader-follower scheme achieved consistency control of multiple agents. The effectiveness of the control scheme is verified through multi-agents trajectory tracking experiments of a networked multi-lighting control system based on a dSPACE controller.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-based Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Nonlinear Systems with Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based active disturbance rejection controller (RL-ADRC) for trajectory tracking control of partially unknown nonlinear systems with external disturbances. It is also a complementary combination of RL and ADRC. In this method, an actor-critic-based RL algorithm is employed to explore an optimal and adaptive control strategy. Unlike traditional ADRC, which requires manual tuning of controller parameters, RL-ADRC utilizes an actor-critic network to approximate the optimal control strategy. By adopting the disturbance compensation philosophy from ADRC and integrating it with RL, RL-ADRC exhibits improved robustness against tracking errors, and the learning process is more efficient in terms of time.

articleTitle: Practical Prescribed-Time Attitude Control for Flexible Spacecraft Based on Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The paper investigates the practical prescribed-time attitude stabilization problem for a flexible spacecraft with unknown disturbances. By introducing a time-varying function, a prescribed-time disturbance observer is designed to estimate the unknown external disturbances. With the aid of the backstepping control method and fully actuated system approach, a practical prescribed-time controller can be proposed by using the disturbance estimation. Theoretical analysis and simulation results prove that the attitude of the flexible spacecraft under the proposed control scheme can converge to prescribed precision within prescribed time.

articleTitle: Finite-Time H∞ Control for a Class of Nonlinear Singular Systems with Static Output Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper designs a static output feedback control law to stabilize nonlinear singular systems in finite-time. Firstly, the finite-time stability of the nonlinear singular system is studied by designing the static output feedback controller. Then, we discuss the finite-time $H_{\infty}$ control problem for nonlinear singular systems under external interference input. Finally, this paper gives a circuit example of a nonlinear singular system for simulation experiments, which indicates the practicability of the feedback control laws.

articleTitle: Fractional-order Command Filter-based Backstepping Control for Nonlinear System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The fractional-order command filter-based backstepping control for trajectory tracking of nonlinear systems is studied in this paper. A fractional-order command filter is established to eliminate the nonlinear chattering phenomenon and avert the issue of complexity explosion. The nonlinear system equips the traditional backstepping control method with fractional calculus, which not only enhances the control effect but also improves the response characteristics of the nonlinear system. Based on the Lyapunov stability, it is proved that the closed-loop nonlinear system is global asymptotic stable. The feasibility and effectiveness of this presented method is proved by the simulation example of a second-order system.

articleTitle: Fault Detection for a Class of Continuous-Time Switched Affine Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this study, the fault detection issue is addressed for a class of continuous-time switched affine systems. The core of our attention is placed on the construction of a fault-detection filter for generating a residual signal that can be analyzed to determine whether or not a fault occurs in the process. More specifically, a full-order switched affine fault detection filter is designed as a residual generator while also provides the essential information for the output feedback switching function. The global asymptotic convergence is ensured for the augmented systems, and the $H_{2}$ performance index is also satisfied. The design conditions are expressed in terms of linear matrix inequalities, which can be solved feasibly by means of readily available tools. The effectiveness of the proposed fault detection filter design method is illustrated via a numerical example.

articleTitle: Three-axes Attitude Maneuvering of Rigid Spacecraft with Two Internal Torques Using Artificial Potential Function
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a control algorithm for underactuated spacecraft with two internal angular momentum exchange devices. In this paper, a geometric constraint of the feasible angular velocity is characterized by the absence of one degree of freedom control torque under the assumption of zero angular momentum of the system, and can be further rendered as a keep-out pointing constraint for attitude dynamics. A special potential function is then proposed for system guidance to evade the unfeasible trajectories while achieving the convergence of the control system to the desired attitude. It is shown that the closed-loop system is ultimately uniformly bounded by the Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to corroborate the effectiveness and performance of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Dissipative Control of Stochastic Markov Jump Systems with Input Saturation and Quantized Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the strictly dissipative control problem for continuous-time stochastic Markov jump systems with input saturation and quantized measurements. A modified sector condition is used to deal with the input saturation. By using a mode-dependent Lyapunov function, new results on the synthesis are proposed with satisfied dissipative performance under a unified convex optimization framework. Finally, simulation studies are conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: Kinematic Analysis and Verification of a 6-DOF Bionic Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of single motion form and poor autonomous operation ability of bionic robot in complex environment, a 6-DOF bionic robot was designed and verified by kinematics simulation. Aiming at the structure of the robot, the theoretical calculation is carried out by MATLAB and the simulation analysis is carried out by ADAMS. According to the simulation results and theoretical calculation results of various actions, the relative error of the displacement variation is no more than 0.07%, and the relative error of the angle variation which proves the correctness of the kinematic modeling with the spinor method. Then, the maximum relative error between the value of each joint variable calculated by algebraic solving methods method and the theoretical given value is 0.0526%, which proves the correctness and effectiveness of the algebraic solving methods. This paper proves that the designed robot can complete a variety of actions with high precision, and also ensures that the designed 6-DOF bionic robot can reach the expected pose, which shows the rationality and high precision of the robot design.

articleTitle: A Maximum Power Point Tracking Control Method for Wind Turbines With Uncertainties Based on Fully Actuated System Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control problem for wind turbine systems with multi-uncertainties is considered. A tracking controller of optimal tip speed ratio is proposed based on fully actuated system (FAS) approach. First, the dynamics of wind turbines in the region below rated wind speed is represented in FAS model. Then, with the analysis of multi-uncertainties in operation of wind turbines, an extended state observer (ESO) is designed to estimate the uncertainties. A controller with uncertainty-compensation ability is proposed based on FAS theory to obtain a closed-loop tracking system of rotor speed with fully actuated characteristics. Theorems are given to show the advantages on stability analysis, parameters selection under constraints and engineering regulation of FAS approach in MPPT control of wind turbines. Finally, an example of 5MW wind turbine of NREL is given for simulation. The results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for MPPT control.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Trajectory Tracking Based on Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Vehicle trajectory tracking is one of the core technologies in the field of automatic driving, various control algorithms are currently used in trajectory tracking. Among existing algorithms, model predictive control (MPC) outperforms other algorithms because it consists of model prediction, receding optimization, and feedback correction. Previous studies have designed trajectory-tracking algorithms under stable road conditions. However, the actual driving scenario is no longer stable, meaning those algorithms may not be applicable. Therefore, we establish a kinematic model for the vehicle with additive noises and propose a trajectory-tracking algorithm based on model predictive control and the extended Kalman filter (EKF). The algorithm can still guarantee real-time calculation and high tracking accuracy under unstable road conditions.

articleTitle: Distributed state and fault estimation of complex networks with time-varying topology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studies the problems of state and fault estimation for a class of discrete-time complex networks with multiplicative fault and time-varying topology. The system state and actuator faults are augmented, and a suitable estimator is designed for each node. In order to obtain a more reliable estimation effect, a distributed estimator is designed, which only relies on information from local node and adjacent nodes. Then, by using inequality technique and mathematical induction, the upper bound of the estimated error covariance is obtained, and the filter gain is calculated to minimize the upper bound. Meanwhile, the filter is designed through solving recursive matrix equation. Besides, a sufficient condition for the existence of estimator is given. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Form of a Class of High-Order Fully Actuated Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Previous works demonstrate the simplicity and convenience of the fully actuated system approach in designing a general controller. However, the replaced variables in the fully actuated system often need an extra calculation, increasing the calculation and simulation complexity in some situations. Thus, this paper proposes an equivalent form of a class of high-order fully actuated systems. The basic deduction procedure of the equivalent form is presented via a typical first-order strict-feedback nonlinear system, and a controller is designed based on the derived form. Like the first-order system, the equivalent forms of a second-order and a high-order strict-feedback system are given directly. An attitude control simulation of rigid spacecraft is presented, indicating the validity and advantage of the proposed form.

articleTitle: Mean Square Exponential Stability of Stochastic Stieltjes Integral Delay Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the mean square exponential stability of a class of stochastic Stieltjes integral delay systems (SSIDSs) is studied. The basic properties and Lyapunov-Krasovskii (L-K) stability theorem with Stieltjes integrals of SSIDSs are discussed firstly. With the help of this theorem, a L-K functional with Stieltjes integrals is introduced to obtain a sufficient stability condition based on linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) by using multiple Jensen inequalities and the nature of stochastic integrals. The use of Stieltjes integrals allows to consider both discrete and distributed delays in the investigated equation. Finally, a numerical example is used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Non-identification Adaptive Output Feedback Control for Nonlinear Systems with Unknown Sensor Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, global adaptive state regulation problem is addressed for a class of nonlinear systems with large unknown measurement sensitivity. Based on a pair of coupled matrix inequalities with an unknown time-varying parameter, a new double-gain (the mix of static and dynamic gains) output feedback controller is presented by combining with an improved dynamic scaling technique. In particular, the control approach proposed uses a non-identification adaptive mechanism and is applicable to a class of nonlinear parametric systems with an unknown constant growth rate. Moreover, our method is non-backstepping and all design parameters are obtained easily.

articleTitle: On Transforming Single Input Linear Time-Varying Systems into High-order Fully Actuated Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: For a linear time-invariant (LTI) system, controllability is equivalent to that it can be transformed into a high-order fully actuated system (HOFA). In this note, it is demonstrated that this is not the case for linear time-varying (LTV) systems even in the single input case. This paper points out that an LTV system can be transformed into a standard HOFA system if and only if its controllability matrix defined in the Silverman criterion is nonsingular for any time, which is only sufficient but not necessary for the controllability of the system. In addition, if the controllability matrix defined in the Silverman criterion is not nonsingular for any time, a degenerated HOFA system might be obtained. Some simple examples are given to demonstrate the reported facts.

articleTitle: Reachable Set Estimation for Nonlinear Switched Singular Systems with Impulsive Perturbation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of reachable set estimation of the nonlinear switched singular system with impulsive perturbation under zero initial conditions and bounded peak disturbance. The objective is to obtain a bounded ellipsoid containing all states from the origin. Firstly, the switched singular system is decomposed into a system consisting of differential and algebraic equations. Secondly, applying the real bounded lemma and integral inequality technique in the framework of the linear matrix inequality (LMI), a sufficient condition for the switched singular system with impulsive perturbation and delay is obtained to ensure that the state trajectory of system is restricted to deriving a closed bounded set from the input with bounded peaks. Finally, the effectiveness of the obtained results in this paper is illustrated by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Online detection method for abnormal states of blast furnace system based on memory and forgetting strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In order to address the problem of abnormal state identification in blast furnace ironmaking process, an improved Mann-Kendall (MK) method is proposed for online abnormal state detection. Firstly, the industrial process of blast furnace ironmaking is analyzed. The silicon content in hot metal is taken as the process vanable, and the time series sampling data of silicon content are obtained by online monitoring. Then, based on the memory and forgetting strategies, the original MK method suitable for single state change point detection is improved to detect multiple abnormal state change points. That is, the change point Satisfying the normal distribution constraints in the online time series are regarded as the abnormal state change point, and the abnormal state change point is memorized as the new starting point of the time series, and all the sampling points before the abnormal state change points are intentionally forgotten. With the continuous extension of silicon content sampling sequence, the multiple normal/abnormal state change points can be detected in real time. Finally, the proposed method is verified by an industrial example, which shows that the proposed method can realize online detection of multiple abnormal states in blast furnace ironmaking.

articleTitle: A Multi-level Feature Extraction Method for Heterogeneous Sample Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The challenge of dealing with small sample sizes is a significant issue in data-driven modeling. To address this challenge, domain adaptation (DA) techniques have been developed to transfer samples from a source domain to a target domain to enhance the sample size. However, in real-world applications, the existing DA methods have limited applicability due to the lack of effective feature extraction approaches. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a novel multi-level feature extraction method for enhancing heterogeneous samples. The proposed method decomposes sample features into three orthogonal dimensions to more accurately express sample information. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms representative methods, highlighting the effectiveness of our approach in addressing the challenges of small sample sizes and domain adaptation.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Prescribed Performance Tracking Control for High-Order Nonlinear Time-Delay Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the tracking control problem of a class of nonlinear high order time-delay systems. The method used to approximate the unknown nonlinear functions is the Radial basis function neural networks (RBFNNs). Then, we propose a feasible adaptive neural tracking control scheme backstepping and prescribed performance technology. The Lyapunov stability theory is applied to ensure that all signals in the closed-loop system are semiglobally uniformly ultimately bounded (SGUUB), and that the tracking error is always kept within the prescribed performance range. The proposed control policy is verified to be effective through simulation results.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Stabilization for a Class of Switched Nonholonomic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of prescribed-time stabilization (PTS) is studied for a class of nonholonomic systems (NSs) with switched chain structures. By suitably introducing the time-varying function into the virtual (actual) controllers, a non-scaling transformation design scheme for state feedback is developed, which forces the states of the closed-loop system (CLS) to zero in any prescribed finite time. Finally, simulation results are given to confirm the efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Adaptive Neural Prescribed Performance Control for Nonlinear MIMO Singularly Perturbed Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the adaptive neural fixed-time prescribed performance control for a class of multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) nonlinear singularly perturbed systems (SPSs). At first, a fixed-time prescribed performance function is introduced to adjust the transient and steady-state performance of the system, which enables the tracking errors can converge to a preassigned area within a given fixed time. Then, by integrating the fixed-time stability and the backstepping control technique, an adaptive neural fixed-time trajectory tracking controller is designed to guarantee that all the signals in the closed-loop system (CLS) are semi-global uniformly ultimately practically fixed-time bounded. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed control approach is verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: Distributed Adaptive Consensus Control for Multiple Simple-pendulum Network Systems with Fault Detection and Isolation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A distributed adaptive consensus tracking control method with fault detection and isolation based on multi-agent systems (MASs) is proposed for multiple simple-pendulum network systems with leader-following mode. Different from previous researches, the proposed method can provide effective control both before and after the failure or loss of partial members. Firstly, in order to detect the existence of faults, dynamic observers are designed to realize the state estimation of followers, in which the design process does not rely on other unknown inputs, this makes the design more concise than those existing results. Secondly, in order to detect fault members accurately and effectively, the adaptive threshold is designed. On this basis, a distributed adaptive consensus protocol is presented to guarantee the fully distributed tracking control for multiple simple-pendulum network systems without depending on the global communication topologies. Finally, the simulation results of multiple simple-pendulum network systems with and without fault verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: A ballistic optimization method with field-of-view angle constraint and impact angle constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Considering the problem that the impact angle constraint may lead to the loss of target field of view, a ballistic optimization method with field of view (FOV) angle constraint and impact angle constraint is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the expression for the FOV angle is obtained using the coordinate transformation relationship and simplified by reasonable assumptions. Secondly, the problem is transformed into an optimal control problem in pitch plane by establishing the integrated model and constraint model of the missile. Finally, the Gaussian pseudo-spectral method is used to solve the problem. The simulation results show that the terminal guidance trajectory satisfying the FOV angle constraint and the impact angle constraint can be obtained by this method.

articleTitle: State estimation of two-dimensional systems with bounded disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper considers the state estimation problem of the two-dimensional Fomasini-Marchesini second (FM-II) model. To deal with the bounded disturbances, the quadratic boundedness is first defined for two-dimensional system described by the FM-II model and then used for the state observer design. By using the invariant set related to the defined quadratic boundedness, the upper bound of the estimation error is obtained, and a criterion for the quadratic stability of the estimation error dynamic systems is proposed. The expected observer gain matrix is obtained via linear matrix inequality technique. Simulation study is provided to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Observer-Based Output Feedback Control of Stochastic Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This article addresses the observer-based output feedback controller synthesis for Ito stochastic nonlinear plants via Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy models. The unavailable system states are detected by designing a fuzzy observer. Based on an advanced matrix inequality, sufficient conditions for controller synthesis are obtained through a linearization procedure. The proposed controller synthesis method allows both the measurement output matrices and control input matrices of each local model to contain parameter uncertainties. Simulation studies are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Tuning Function-Based Prescribed Performance Control of Nonlinear Systems With Discontinuous References
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper is dealt with the problem of prescribed performance control (PPC) for the strict-feedback systems with piecewise continuous references. The discontinuity of the reference results in the abrupt variations of the tracking error and the intermediate errors, which renders the existing PPC designs challenging. To overcome this difficulty, a tuning function-based approach to adapting the performance funnels is proposed. In this way, the performance functions are reasonably modified in accordance with the discontinuity of the errors, such that all the errors converge to the predefined bounds in the given time after the discontinuity occurs. Moreover, this approach is compatible with the standard PPC method in the sense that it preserves the inherent robustness of PPC against the model uncertainties of the system. Despite unknown nonlinearities, there is no need to employ neural networks or fuzzy logic systems for approximation. The simulation results on a single-link robotic manipulator illustrate the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Data-Driven Learning Load Frequency Control for Nonlinear Power Systems with Repetitive Electric Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Energy-intensive (EI) enterprise power system is an important part of energy interconnection networks, and their short-term industrial electricity loads exhibit a typical cyclic behavior. In order to address the problem of frequency stability for EI enterprise power systems with the unknown model, a load frequency control (LFC) scheme based on an adaptive neural data-driven learning algorithm is proposed. Firstly, an equivalent iterative dynamic data model between frequency deviation and input/output information is established. Subsequently, a linear parameterized learning controller is developed based on dynamic linearization technology, which reduces the dependence of controller design on accurate models. Meanwhile, the pseudo-partial learning gain is continuously and adaptively updated by an RBF neural network approximator. In addition, the convergence of the system is proved by the Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, a simulation example is given.

articleTitle: Building Energy Allocation Using Distributed Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a distributed energy allocation strategy for energy shortage scenarios is proposed. Users are allowed to set the priority order so that the proposed strategy is able to meet the urgent needs. A building model containing three zones is created in Energyplus and the strategy is deployed in Matlab.By introducing Mle+, a joint simulation of MATLAB and Energyplus is implemented. Centralized, decentralized and distributed model predictive control are applied to the energy shortage scenario respectively, and the results show that our approach can satisfy the urgent need for energy supply.

articleTitle: Robust Trajectory Tracking Control for Quadrotor UAV with External Disturbances via Fully Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust trajectory tracking control strategy based on the high-order fully actuated system approach and disturbance observer. In spite of the strong coupling characteristic and high nonlinearity of the quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (QUAV) system, the linear time-invariant system with desired eigenstructures can be obtained by designing a greatly simple robust controller via the direct parametric method. Meanwhile, a disturbance observer (DO) is designed to estimate the external disturbances, and the output of the DO can be adapted for the controller design to compensate for the affect of external disturbances on control performance. Eventually, the numerical simulation results of the QUAV trajectory tracking demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed robust control scheme.

articleTitle: A Fully-Actuated System Approach for Manipulator Systems with External Disturbance and Actuator Saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Disturbance rejection control has been a hot issue in the field of manipulator control, especially for nonlinear systems, because it is difficult to achieve global stability, and the expected design purpose may not be achieved. In the current control field, the second-order manipulator system is generally converted into the first-order system, which will damage the fully actuated characteristics of the system. In this paper, a controller is designed for the manipulator system with actuator saturation based on the fully-actuated system approach. By canceling the dynamic characteristics of the open-loop system, a closed-loop system with desired characteristics can be obtained, and the stabilization control of the manipulator system is realized. At the same time, the performance index of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> problem is solved. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fault estimation and fault tolerant control of uncertain networked predictive control systems under actuator faults
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The fault estimation and fault tolerant control problems of networked discrete-time uncertain control systems with stochastic time delay and actuator faults are addressed in this paper. Firstly, a predictive control law that achieves reliable control performance in the presence of communication constraints is introduced. Based on the networked predictive control approach, an active fault-tolerant control strategy for networked discrete-time uncertain control systems with actuator faults is proposed. The strategy consists of three parts: an observer to estimate the state, a predictive controller to generate a fault-tolerant control signal sequence, and a networked delay compensator to actively compensate for the network-induced delay. Under the dual influence of time delay and actuator faults, the fault tolerant control protocol can keep the system stable. Digital simulation results clarify the method.

articleTitle: Event-triggered PMI Extended Kalman Filter and Its Application to Sensor Fault Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the event-triggered fault estimation (FE) problem in combination with extended Kalman filter (EKF) and proportional gain and multi-integral (PMI) techniques. A nonlinear system with sensor fault is transformed into an augmented discrete time model, where the fault signal is described in the form of polynomials. Based on this, a new event-triggered fault estimator is designed for the augmented system so that the generated estimation error is completely decoupled from the event-triggered transmission error. In addition, the FE issue for nonlinear system is converted into the design of the estimator gain matrix, which is addressed by minimizing the estimation error covariance. Finally, a simulation study based on a three-tank system is presented to verify the applicability of the developed scheme, by comparing with the existing event-triggered EKF schemes for FE.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Dynamic Output Feedback Control of Positive Markov Jump Systems under Denial-of-Service Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studies the design of event-triggered dynamic output feedback controllers for continuous-time positive Markov jump systems subject to unknown periodic denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. First, the attack signal is given. According to the characteristics of DoS attacks, the event-triggered condition is divided into two parts: the form of 1-norm during the attacks sleep and the end time of the attacks. Then, according to the two states of the attacks, the systems are modeled as positive Markov jump systems with switching form, that is, the open-loop systems with attacks and the closed-loop systems without attacks. Next, the event-triggered dynamic output feedback controller is designed to ensure the positivity and stability of the systems. At the same time, it is proved that there is no Zeno phenomenon. All results in this paper are described by linear programming. Finally, the effectiveness and practicability of the results are illustrated by simulation.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Algorithm Based on Ant Colony and Genetic Algorithm for AUV Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid algorithm based on ant colony optimization (ACO) and genetic algorithm(GA) is proposed for path planning of an autonomous underwater vehicle. The novel algorithm, which combines ACO and GA has the following features: ❨1❩ It plans path through ACO; ❨2❩ GA is used to find the optimal path; ❨3❩ A new evaluation function is proposed and is adjusted to select a relatively smooth path; ❨4❩ The number of search points is reduced to reduce computation load. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can find shorter paths in the same map compared with ACO.

articleTitle: Direct Force Sliding Mode Attitude Control based on Fully Actuated System Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The switching direct force device, which is a typical nonlinear control system, controls the attitude of projectile body. Therefore, a new design of direct force attitude control based on the theory of all-wheel drive system, which is more convenient than traditional methods in control parameters configuration, is carried out in this paper. In order to design the control parameters, the missile body model is transformed into a high-order fully actuated system based on fully actuated system theory. An improved pulse modulator is designed by differential tracker to obtain the angular acceleration information required by the fully actuated system. Sliding mode control is used to further improve the system performance in order to adapt to the uncertainties of the control system. Stability of this control system is proved by constructing the Lyapunov function. According to the result of simulation, it showed that steady-state error is reduced from 1° to 0.2° in comparison to PSR modulator when the thrust was deflected by 30% under the premise of ensuring the dynamic performance of the control system, which significantly improve the control accuracy.

articleTitle: Body Structure Constraint For 3D Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: 2D to 3D pose lifting is a promising method in 3D human pose estimation, and exciting improvement has been achieved after Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) is introduced into this task. In this paper, we propose a training method that achieved symmetry constraints of the skeleton, and it works well combined with different lifting methods. To make full use of the connection relationship of the joints, we propose a novel GL-Net, which views the human skeleton as a graph, for lifting 2D pose to 3D. Then, we add a Body factor Net to extract features from the 2D human pose estimation networks for correcting the scale of the 3D skeleton. We validate our method on public datasets. Experiments show that our model makes great progress. The proposed lifting method should be a promising tool for accurate 3D human pose estimation.

articleTitle: Event-triggered finite-time stabilization of maglev system with suspension air gap constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the finite-time stabilization of maglev system with suspension air gap limitation utilizing event-triggered technique. A subtle event-triggered controller is constructed on the basis of a finite-time trigger mechanism with a time-varying threshold and tangential barrier function. This control algorithm ensures that the suspension air gap is limited to a specific vicinity while the states of the maglev system converge to the origin within a finite time. The contribution lies in the fact that the resources consuming is reducing effectively while the design and the theory analysis for the constrained and unconstrained suspension air gap are unified. Finally, the practical simulation validates the efficiency and superiority of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Study on Gear Inhibition Strategy of Single Hub Multi-Gear 3DHT
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The working principle of the transmission system is mainly analyzed. Calculate the logical relationship of gear unavailable: calculate the actual gear position and abnormal gear position according to the information of the position sensor, the speed sensor and the current sensor of the gear shifting motor; According to the input shaft speed sensor and P3 speed sensor, the gears with excessive slip and speed are calculated. According to Pl speed sensor, the gear position leading to low engine speed is calculated. The proposed gear inhibition strategy calculates the target gear suppressed according to the actual gear, abnormal gear, gear with excessive slip, gear with too high speed and gear with too low engine speed. The control strategy model and fault injection simulation platform were established using Simulink/ TargetLink. Through the simulation analysis of the proposed gear inhibition strategy and the analysis of the test results, it is shown that the proposed gear inhibition strategy based on different actual current gear positions can effectively avoid unreasonable gear positions and ensure the transmission running in a reasonable range of gear positions.

articleTitle: Global prescribed-time regulation of the chain of integrators subject to external disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studies the global prescribed-time regulation problem for the chain of integrators subject to matched disturbances. New integral controllers consisting of an integral dynamic are proposed to make all states of the systems bounded and prescribed-time convergent to zero. First, by introducing an integral dynamic and a novel state transformation, the chain of integrators with disturbances are converted into a class of generalized feedback nonlinear systems with mismatched disturbances. Second, by virtue of the dynamic gain technique, the problem of designing prescribed-time regulating controllers for the generalized feedback nonlinear systems is transformed into that of designing a dynamic parameter for a class of new systems. At last, following Lyapunov stability theorem and the characteristic of the dynamic parameter, the boundness of the new systems yields the prescribed-time regulation of the generalized feedback nonlinear systems, which indicates the global prescribed-time regulation of the considered systems. The effectiveness of integral controllers is illustrated from simulation results.

articleTitle: Fault feature extraction of rolling bearing based on GWO optimized SVMD
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Rolling bearings typically operate in tough and complex working environments, and the fault pulse characteristics implied in the vibration signals are frequently interfered with by random noise, making fault feature extraction difficult. To address this issue, this paper provides a fault feature extraction method based on the Grey Wolf algorithm (GWO) for optimizing Successive Variational Mode Decomposition (SVMD,). This method uses the minimum fuzzy entropy as the fitness function of the GWO and employs the GWO to adaptively iteratively search for the optimal SVMD balance parameter for signal decomposition, before selecting the Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) with the maximum kurtosis as the target IMF and performing envelope demodulation analysis on it to accurately extract fault feature information. The suggested method outperforms unoptimized SVMD and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) algorithms in terms of computing efficiency and can highlight fault feature components, and the experimental results validate the GWO-SVMD algorithm suggested in this paper.

articleTitle: Super-twisting Sliding Mode Control Based on RBF Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The problems of model uncertainty and complex interference exist in the near space vehicle. The control system needs to anti-interference and adapt to the changes of system parameters while ensuring the rapidity. Therefore, a super-twisting sliding mode control method based on RBF neural network is proposed. RBF neural network can estimate the uncertainties in the system model, design the adaptive law of single parameter through the minimum parameter learning method, which ensures the demand of real-time control. The super-twisting sliding mode control with strong robustness can effectively suppress disturbance and estimation error of the neural network, and can weaken the chattering phenomenon. Lyapunov stability theory proves the stability of the closed-loop system. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is verified by digital simulation.

articleTitle: Delayed Recoil Control of Deepwater Drilling Riser Systems via A Non-Small Delay Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper considers the delayed recoil control problem of deepwater riser systems by a non-small delay approach. A velocity feedback controller with interval-like time-varying input delay is proposed to attain the suppression effect of the frictional disturbance on recoil responses. The main difference from the existing results lies in two aspects: a delayed static output feedback controller is designed with partially measurable velocity information, and a non-small delay method instead of small delay method is attempted for solving the control problem. Some interval-delay-dependent criteria of $H_{\infty}$ performance analysis and control design are derived. Simulation results are given to verify the effectiveness and advantages of the delayed recoil control method.

articleTitle: Antiswing Sliding Mode Control of Overhead Cranes with a Finite-Time Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, based on a finite-time disturbance observer, a sliding mode control strategy is proposed for the antiswing control of overhead cranes, which can easily deal with the presence of unpredictable disturbances. To be specific, the original crane model firstly is transformed into a chained form. Then, with the help of finite-time observer, a novel nonlinear controller is designed to regulate the trolley to the desired position and realize the antiswing control of payload, while also avoiding chattering and singularity. Additionally, Lyapunov techniques are utilized to guarantee the performance of the closed-loop system. Finally, experimental results are used to verify the effectiveness of the suggested method.

articleTitle: Research on Unrelated Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem Considering Machine Eligibility
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Consider an unrelated parallel machine scheduling problems with machine eligibility, where each processed workpiece can only be arranged on specific machines for processing. In this paper, we propose a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm which introduces an elite reverse learning strategy and sine and cosine optimization algorithm to minimize the maximum completion time. In this algorithm, the elite reverse learning strategy is introduced heuristically to provide better feasible solutions for the algorithm randomization, thus accelerating the convergence rate. In addition, the sine and cosine optimization algorithm is introduced in the particle iteration process to update the velocity vector of the particle swarm, so as to enhance the diversity of the population. The effectiveness and advantage of the new PSO in solving the problem are verified by simulation experiments and comparation with other algorithms.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ Control of Polynomial Fuzzy Singular Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This study examines the polynomial fuzzy singular systems (PFSS) stability problem. Based on singular nonlinear systems, a polynomial fuzzy model is created, and the stability of the system is examined using a suitable Lyapunov function. The sufficient condition for the system impulse controllable is investigated, and the system’s stabilization and robust $H_{\infty}$ control problems are discussed. Different from the existed conclusions, the controller has a simple structure and can be designed and applied to more PFSS.

articleTitle: Fully Actuated System Approach Based Tracking Control of Space Manipulator with An Optimal Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper deals with the tracking problem of a space manipulator in the presence of actuator saturation. A tracking error system is first derived in the form of fully actuated system (FAS) model. Based on the FAS approach, a tracking controller is designed for the space manipulator, which makes the closed-loop system a constant linear one with an arbitrarily assigned eigenstructure. Then, in the framework of parametric method, the control gain matrices are determined by employing the optimal parameter tuning method with satisfying the input saturation constraint. Finally, a numerical simulation is performed to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Detection methods of surface defects of sintering material based on machine vision
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The iron and steel industry is one of the pillar industries in the national economy. Blast furnace (BF) ironmaking is the core step in long-process ironmaking. Before BF production, to improve the ore quality, sintering is adopted to provide high-quality man-made ore from raw materials. In the sintering process, the material surface state is the main indicator for monitoring the ignition effect. During the actual production process, due to the influence of the ingredients and the ignition effect, there are defects on the sintering material surface, including yellow mud, mouse holes, and cracks. Detection of defect information on the material surface is conducive to ensuring the stable quality of the sinter and the stable operation of sintering production. This paper designs the corresponding detection methods for the three defects based on machine vision algorithms, 1) Yellow mud detection: separate the material surface area of the sintering trolley by semantic segmentation, and judge whether there is yellow mud according to the HSV histogram correlation combined with the shape judgment condition of yellow mud; 2) Mouse hole detection: use the target detection method of YOLOv5 without Mosaic detects mouse holes and improves the detection ability of small targets; 3) Crack detection: transfer learning and improved DeepLabv3+ network semantic segmentation are used for crack detection to improve the accuracy of crack detection. Finally, all methods are applied to the actual production line, and the detection accuracy and effectiveness of the above methods are verified through image testing and calculation of evaluation indicators, which can meet the needs of on-site use.

articleTitle: Adaptive fixed-time output feedback fault tolerant control for input-quantized perturbed planar nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The problem of output feedback control for a class of input-quantized perturbed planar nonlinear systems with multiple faults and uncertain parameters is investigated under the fixed time convergence scheme. Different from the existing works on the finite-time fault tolerant schemes and deterministic system stabilization strategies, this paper consider the novel adaptive parameter compensation method to accommodate the unknown actuator faults and the the hysteresis quantizer parameters in fixed time. In order to solve the full state measurable limited problem, the fixed-time observer scheme is proposed by using the the bi-limit homogeneity technique. Finally, the global practically fixed-time stability of the adaptive output feedback FTC systems is proved by adaptive back-stepping technique and Lyapunov theory analysis.

articleTitle: High-order Fully Actuated Control Approach for Flexible Servo Systems Using Dynamical Compensator
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-order fully actuated (HOFA) control approach for flexible servo (FS) systems using dynamical compensator. The FS system belongs to a class of underactuated mechanical systems. Its dynamics can be described by a classical two-mass system (TMS) model, which is transformed into an HOFA model by variable elimination. With the full-actuation feature, the control law can be directly obtained in an extremely simple and straightforward way for a desired closed-loop system. Moreover, dynamical compensator is designed to attenuate the effect of unknown disturbances such that the control accuracy can be further improved. The system stability is analyzed in the presence of uncertainties. Comparative experiments are carried out on an FS system driven by PMSM to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based Event-Triggered Adaptive Containment Control for Switched Nonlinear Multi-agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This article is related to the event-triggered adaptive containment control problem for switched nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs), in which the nonlinear functions are completely unknown. Under this difficulty, radial basis function neural networks (RBF NNs) are used to approximate the unknown nonlinear functions. Besides, an adaptive containment control scheme with the relative threshold event-triggered control (ETC) mechanism is constructed, which can alleviate the communication burden. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, it is shown that all the signals in the closed-loop MASs are semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded (SGUUB). Meanwhile, based on the proposed adaptive containment control strategy, it can ensure that all the outputs of the followers eventually enter the convex set spanned by the leaders’. Finally, the simulation results are presented to illustrate the availability of control protocol.

articleTitle: Controllability of Multi-agent Systems over Finite Fields Based on High-order Fully Actuated System Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the controllability of multi-agent systems over finite fields is studied based on the high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approaches. The HOFA system over finite fields is presented first. The necessary and sufficient conditions for the controllability of linear systems over finite fields are given in terms of the controllability matrix. It is proved that a linear system over a finite field is controllable if and only if it can be transformed into an HOFA system. Finally, an example is shown to verify the validity of the main results of this paper.

articleTitle: Stabilization Control for Stochastic High-order Fully-actuated Systems with Persistent Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Following the high-order fully actuated (HOFA) systems proposed by Prof. GR Duan, stochastic high-order fully actuated (SHOFA) systems were also developed to consider the stochastic disturbances. However, existing studies require that disturbances disappear at the equilibrium point, which limits the applicability of the method. This paper proposes a novel control scheme to stabilize the SHOFA systems with persistent disturbances. The characterization of SHOFA systems is analyzed utilizing the concepts of probabilistic ultimate bounds and probabilistic invariant sets. Therefore, the quantitative control indices in probability are available under general probability distributions. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified in the simulation.

articleTitle: A Fully-actuated System Approach for Spacecraft Attitude Control with Input Saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the attitude control problem for a rigid spacecraft subject to external disturbances and actuator saturation. A novel control scheme is technically proposed by incorporating the Nussbaum gain technique and extended state observer into the fully-actuated system theory. First, a fully-actuated system model for the attitude error dynamics is established. Then, the Nussbaum gain technique is employed to tackle the time-varying input gains arising from input saturation, and an extended state observer is introduced to estimate and compensate system uncertainties and external disturbances. The stability of the closed-loop system and the convergence of state errors are accordingly proven via Lyapunov stability approaches. Finally, a numerical simulation is carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Finite-time Attitude Tracking for Fully-actuated Flexible Spacecraft without Angular Velocity Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of finite-time attitude control for fully-actuated flexible spacecraft subject to external disturbance and vibration of flexible appendages without angular velocity measurements is investigated. Firstly, a nonlinear finite-time angular velocity observer with dynamic parameters is proposed to estimate the unknown angular velocity. Then, an adaptive disturbance observer is designed to estimate the lumped disturbance which contains the external disturbance, vibration of flexible appendages and observation errors of the angular velocity observer in finite time. Next, utilizing the reconstructed information from the observers, a novel integral sliding mode (ISM) and a velocity-free attitude tracking controller are presented to achieve attitude tacking in finite-time without chatting problem. The main feature of the designed control algorithm is that the unknown angular velocity, external disturbance, and vibration of flexible appendages are addressed simultaneously without awareness of the boundary of the unknown lumped disturbance. Rigorous Lyapunov-based analyses show that the finite-time ultimately bounded stability of the observation errors and tracking errors can be guaranteed under the designed control law. Finally, numerical simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed observer-based attitude control scheme.

articleTitle: Matrix Approach to Finding Recurrent State Equilibrium of State-based Games
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: State-based games are an extension of normal games since an underlying state space is introduced, and the equilibrium in state-based games is called recurrent state equilibrium (RSE). How to find RSE of state-based games is a challenging issue. The process of finding RSE includes two steps. Firstly, find the pure Nash equilibria of state-invariant games for each state in the state space. In this step, the basic tool is the semi-tensor product of matrices. Secondly, for each pure Nash equilibrium of state-invariant game, calculate the recurrent classes of state transition process. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is presented for the existence of RSE, and an algorithm is developed for finding RSE.

articleTitle: RoD-Based Rigid Formation Control of Nonlinear Uncertain Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this note, we research a class of rigid formation control by employing ratio-of-distance (RoD) rigidity theory. We construct multi-agent target formation shapes via RoD-based rigid frameworks, while nonlinear uncertainties are thoroughly considered in multi-agent system dynamics. Our study focuses on designing adaptive rigid formation controllers to drive all agents to acquire and maintain target formation shapes, and meanwhile make aH agents keep maneuvering at target velocities. We consider two cases that target velocities are time-invariant and time-varying. Since time-varying maneuvering case is special that controllers in time-invariant maneuvering case cannot be used, nonsmooth analysis based on differential inclusion theory is employed to design new controllers which are nonsmooth to realize control objectives.

articleTitle: A new lateral semi-active control strategy for the railway vehicle with built-in bogies based on fully-actuated system approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Compared with the traditional railway vehicle with built-out bogies, the advantages of the railway vehicle with built-in bogies are lightweight with lower wheel rail force and stronger curve passing ability, etc. But it also has the downside of deterioration of lateral comfort. In order to improve the lateral vibration of the railway vehicle with built-in bogies, a new semi-active control strategy is proposed in this paper. Firstly, borrowing from fully-actuated system approaches, a robust controller with state feedback is designed to calculate the desired control force; then a state observer is designed based on the Kalman filtering principle, which is used to estimate the lateral vibration state of the car body; finally, a damping force controller is designed to calculate the command current to track the desired force. Simulation results indicate that, the root-mean-square values of lateral acceleration and lateral ride index of the car body are improved significantly with the proposed semi-active suspension. Therefore, this paper provides a new strategy for the lateral vibration control of the railway vehicle with built-in bogies.

articleTitle: Attitude Control of Underactuated Quadrotor UAV Based on Improved ADRC
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a cascaded control framework based on active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is proposed for underactuated quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to improve the stability of attitude control and the ability of anti-disturbance. The model of quadrotor is given in the first, and then the improved active disturbance rejection control is applied into angular speed controller, the improved nonlinear extended state observer (NLESO) not only considering the delay of motor but also using a smooth nonlinear function which enhanced the accuracy of state estimation. The simulation results show that the improved ADRC performs better in both of the ability of attitude tracking and the ability of anti-disturbance.

articleTitle: Defects Clustering for Mineral Sintering Surface Based on Multi-source Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: During sintering of minerals, multiple categories of defects often appear on the surface of material due to hysteresis of control. Fusion of data from multiple sources is considered in this paper in a bid to identify different types of defects and to improve the utilization of collected data. Specifically, this paper establishes a heterogeneous multi-source dataset based on sintering data. And a novel deep learning approach for multi-source data fusion is introduced and extended. Based on constructed multi-source dataset and associated algorithm, the downstream task of clustering is carried out. Affiliated experimental results show that the multi-source information clustering process for mineral sintered surface defects proposed in this paper outperforms unimodal approach, and relative performance metrics have reached the level of engineering applications.

articleTitle: Safety-Guaranteed Control for Fly-Around with Noncooperative Space Target via a Fully-Actuated System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A safety-guaranteed control method based on fully-actuated system theory is proposed in this work for a service spacecraft flying around a noncooperative target with undesired orbital maneuvers. Firstly, the fly-around relative motion dynamic equations are established and transformed into a fully-actuated system form. An initial control law is then designed on basis of the fully-actuated system theory. To continue, a nonlinear manifold is constructed and constrained by the appointed-time performance functions to prescribe the control performance, and an intermediate control law is proposed to realize the fly-around objectives. Finally, a group of numerical simulation are organized to verify the feasibility of the proposed method and its robustness against undesired orbital maneuvers.

articleTitle: TP Mode Transformation based UAV Control Method with Hesitant Fuzzy Sets
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A tensor product (TP) mode transformation-based intelligent control method is presented in this paper by using the hesitant fuzzy set to make decisions to decide which controller can be used by the control system. One of the aims of extending the TP mode transformation (TPMT) based method is to form a new type of fuzzy controller by using the hesitant degree of hesitant fuzzy sets. To improve the degree of intelligence of the fuzzy control method, hesitant fuzzy sets are utilized to augment the generated models, and then a hesitant fuzzy TPMT-based controller for UAV systems is presented. At last, the newly proposed controller is evaluated using simulation results.

articleTitle: Multi-Robot Motion Planning: A Learning-Based Artificial Potential Field Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Motion planning is a crucial aspect of robot autonomy as it involves identifying a feasible motion path to a destination while taking into consideration various constraints, such as input, safety, and performance constraints, without violating either system or environment boundaries. This becomes particularly challenging when multiple robots run without communication, which compromises their real-time efficiency, safety, and performance. In this paper, we present a learning-based potential field algorithm that incorporates deep reinforcement learning into an artificial potential field (APF). Specifically, we introduce an observation embedding mechanism that pre-processes dynamic information about the environment and develop a soft wall-following rule to improve trajectory smoothness. Our method, while belonging to reactive planning, implicitly encodes environmental properties. Additionally, our approach can scale up to any number of robots and has demonstrated superior performance compared to APF and RL through numerical simulations.
