Finally, experiments are conducted to highlight the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A Double-Mode-Dependent Event-Triggered Control Scheme for Asynchronous Switched Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a double-mode-dependent event-triggered mechanism (ETM) to deal with the exponential stabilization issue of asynchronous switched linear systems. Considering that the system state cannot be fully obtained, a state observer is designed. The ETM incorporates the observer state, a triggering upper bound and a jump function together to compensate for the asynchronous switching case. Comprehensive consideration of the designed ETM and the observer state, an augmented system model is established. In comparison with previous studies that impose a limit on system switching times within the triggering interval, zero trigger and p triggers within a switching interval of the system are both considered. The exponential stabilization is studied based on double-mode-dependent multiple Lyapunov functions and the average dwell time (ADT). Meanwhile, an algorithm for the observer gain and triggering parameter are given. Besides, it proves that the minimum triggering interval is greater than zero, thus avoiding the Zeno behavior. Finally, numerical results are given to illustrate the validity and practicability of this method.

articleTitle: LPV Gain-Scheduled Output-Feedback Tracking Control for PMSMs with Inexact Rotor Position Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel gain-scheduled output-feedback (GSOF) controller is designed to address the rotor speed tracking issue for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) with inexact rotor position measurement. The PMSMs speed tracking control issue is transformed to study the LPV system control design issue in nonlinear torque modulation without direct-quadrature transformation. By choosing the rotor position as scheduling parameters, a kind of LPV GSOF controller is proposed to stabilize the tracking error system. Affected by external disturbances or faults in the position sensors, exact values of rotor position may not be available for the design of LPV GSOF controller. By using the Lyapunov function approach, sufficient conditions with less conservatism are obtained with the line search, such that the corresponding error systems are globally uniformly exponentially stable and satisfy an upper bound of $l_{2}$-gain performance indexes. Finally, the effectiveness and applicability of the developed approaches are validated via a class of PMSMs system.

articleTitle: Dynamic Composite Multi-Source Bumpless Transfer Control for Mass-Switched Unmanned Marine Vehicles of Dynamic Positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This article studies the networked unmanned marine vehicles (UMVs) of dynamic positioning (DP) based on mass-switched with dynamic composite multi-source bumpless transfer (DCMSBT) performance. First, the model of the mass-switched system of networked UMVs based on the quantizer mechanism is established. Second, a kind of DCMSBT control related to the variation of bump value is introduced into the switched UMVs system model. Third, a control strategy is proposed to achieve the DP of UMVs with multiple disturbances based on a joint design of a disturbance observer, the desired controller, event-triggered schemes and a switching rule. Finally, a UMVs of DP example proves the method works.

articleTitle: Adaptive Consensus for Uncertain MIMO Multi-Agent Systems over a Directed Graph Interacting only Relative Output Information
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the consensus problem for uncertain multi-input multi-output (MIMO) multi-agent systems (MASs) over a directed graph. An observer-based output feedback adaptive control algorithm is constructed, which interacts only relative output information of neighboring agents. In particular, Luenberger-like state observers and reference models are designed for the agents to deal with inaccessible states and the uncertainties. Based on the strictly positive real (SPR) method and the Lyapunov stability theory, the consensus convergence is proved. Finally, a numerical example is presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Bayesian Estimation for Linear Dynamical Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper presents a robust Bayesian approach for identification of linear dynamical systems (LDS) with non-Gaussian observation noises. The Bayesian treatment of the identification problem is formulated by introducing suitable likelihood functions and prior information. The posterior distributions over unknown parameters and hidden states are jointly estimated under variational Bayesian (VB) framework, where the augmentation technique is adopted to make inference of the LDS with random parameters, and the parameter uncertainties can be also quantified by the variance statistics. Numerical studies are performed to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: T-S-Fuzzy-Model-Based Output Feedback Steering Control in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, a model predictive controller based on T-S fuzzy model is investigated for the path-tracking of autonomous vehicles. Due to complicated road conditions, it is the case that the vehicle velocity changes during cruising, and moreover, some physical states of the vehicle are unavailable for control. By adopting fuzzy modeling techniques, a T-S fuzzy model of the vehicle lateral dynamics is proposed by considering the varying longitudinal velocities. The robust positively invariant (RPI) set for the state estimation error and observer gain are determined through offline computation, then a fuzzy model predictive controller is derived by solving a Min-max optimization problem. Finally, some validation results with Car-sim/Simulink joint simulation are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Optimal Control for Discrete-Time Step Backward High-Order Fully Actuated Models
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper concerns the optimal control problem for dynamic systems represented by the discrete-time step backward high-order fully actuated (HOFA) models. A quadratic performance index of the system states is first proposed, and then for the finite-time output tracking problem and the infinite-time output regulation problem, the corresponding optimal controllers in the state feedback form are obtained as a combination of two sub-controllers: one is designed by utilizing the inherent full-actuation feature of the HOFA model to covert the original model into a linear constant model, while the other is further designed for this converted linear constant model to minimize the quadratic performance index. Finally, two simulation examples are provided to illustrate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed optimal controllers.

articleTitle: Dual performance Stackelberg game for unknown nonlinear system with saturating input constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the dual performance $\mathrm{H}_{2} / \mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ optimization problem for the nonlinear system with constrained input is solved. The hierarchical multi-player control is described in the framework of the Stackelberg game. The control input and the external disturbance are deemed as the leader and follower, which makes the individual decisions in different levels. Thus the hierarchical control is considered as a two-stage optimization problem. The coupled hierarchical leader-follower Hamilton-Jacobi(HJ) equations with considering the saturating and costate constraints are derived. The existence of the Stackelberg equilibrium is supplied. To avoid the requirement of the internal drift dynamic, a hierarchical integral learning algorithm is proposed for solving the dual performance problem, where the constraints are considered in the iteration steps. A single critic Neural Network(NN) is built to accomplish the designed learning scheme and lessen the computation burden. A nonlinear simulation example with considering the saturating input bound is given to show the effectiveness of the addressed online learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Unstructured Small Target Obstacle Detection Technology on Lunar Surface Driven by Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Unstructured pavement features during lunar patrol pose a great threat to the safety of the rover, rocks and pits and other small targets may cause the rover to overturn or wheel trap, and at present, these small targets in the weak texture of the lunar environment has the problem of small number of pixels, small gradient resulting in difficult detection, this paper proposes a lightweight recognition network model based on variant yolo, first collect lunar surface environment images to make custom datasets, including data screening, annotation, calibration and image enhancement. Finally, the three improved algorithms based on attention mechanism and benchmark algorithms are experimentally verified on the target detection dataset of the star surface environment and the outdoor environment, and finally the YOLOv5-ECA algorithm with the highest mAP value is selected as the object detection algorithm in this paper, which can achieve obstacle detection of real-time rapid response to obstacle detection in the promising spaceborne computing power environment in the future.

articleTitle: Model-Free Spacecraft Attitude Fault-Tolerant Control Based on Adaptive Iterative Fuzzy Kinky Inference
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Aiming at the precision control problem of spacecraft attitude dynamics with actuator faults, a model-free adaptive approach is proposed to the control scheme design. Utilizing the I/O measurement of the spacecraft attitude, the controller is derived by the discrete time data driven iteration without accurate dynamic model. To deal with nonlinear uncertainties which cannot be suppressed by the nominal model-free adaptive controller, an fuzzy logic-based adaptive iterative prediction is carried out on the basis of the kinky inference learning rule when there is insufficient prior data. Stability analysis of the attitude tracking error, uncertainties prediction and other close-loop signals are discussed with the aid of contraction mapping principle. Simulation results with the comparison of adaptive extended state observer based data driven control strategy and general kinky inference learning rule demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in this work.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of a 6DOF Spacecraft on Lie Group SE(3)
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the attitude and orbit tracking control of a rigid spacecraft with input constraints. The six degree-of-freedom (DOF) maneuvers of the spacecraft are described in the framework of Lie group $SE(3)$. With the aid of the discrete Lagrange-d’Alembert principle, the Lie group variational integrator (LGVI) is designed to discretize the translation and orientation motion on $SE(3)$. Then, based on the derived discrete model, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) scheme on $SE(3)$ is proposed to steer the spacecraft to track the desired attitude and orbit. In each prediction horizon, the infinite time optimization problem is converted into a finite time optimization problem to be solved. Moreover, terminal inequality constraint and terminal cost function are introduced to guarantee the stability of the closed-loop system. Finally, the effectiveness and good performance of the proposed control law are validated by numerical simulation. The simulation results indicate that the approach developed in this study not only naturally preserves the Lie group structure of the system, but effectively improves computational accuracy.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Tolerance for High-order Fully-actuated Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In the paper, a novel fault-tolerant controller is presented for high-order fully-actuated systems (HOFASs) with sensor faults. Nonlinear controllable HOFASs can be globally stabilized via specific control laws. An observability normal form based on each individual measurement is utilized to deduce a q-redundant observation proposition of the HOFAS model with nonlinear measurements. Then, the proposed sensor fault tolerance approach based on redundant observability can yield the ultimately uniformly bounded stability. Main results are proved theoretically and illustrated experimentally.

articleTitle: A Smoothing and Mapping Tightly Coupled Multi-modal Fusion Autonomous Navigation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The planetary surface environment is unstructured with strong light, strong shadows, weak texture and many fluctuations. The special circumstances result in dim light or overexposure, lack of perceptual features, and no GPS or prior information support, which brings great challenges to the robust navigation of the planetary rover in the motion and jolt state. In dim light environment, it is difficult for a single camera to provide highly reliable feature recognition and tracking. Meanwhile, in unstructured similar environment, it is difficult for a single lidar to provide high fidelity depth measurement and motion estimation. In this paper, a multi-factor graph optimization model based on inertial system (IMU) is constructed, and a smoothing and mapping tightly coupled multi-modal fusion autonomous navigation method is proposed. With IMU as the central node, the visual inertia odometer (VIO) and laser inertia odometer (LIO) subsystems optimize the state pose in a tightly coupled way, which can effectively constrain the deviation drift of IMU. Moreover, the system introduces the rut line, terrain skyline and other line features as well as historical environmental information feedback. Reliably navigation can be achieved even if the visual or laser factor is failed or restarted. The measured data of obstacle simulation field show that the autonomous navigation method proposed in this paper can achieve high precision and robust real-time state estimation and map construction under the condition of high-speed motion and jolt.

articleTitle: The Local and Remote Stochastic Nonzero-sum Game for Multiplicative Noise Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the local and remote stochastic nonzero-sum game for a multiplicative noise system with inconsistent information structure is investigated, which multiplicative noise can cause nonlinear characteristics of linear systems, making it difficult to calculate the optimal estimator and the optimal linear feedback Nash equilibrium. For the local and remote stochastic nonzero-sum game, the local player and remote player can access different information, and each player is designed to minimize its own cost function. The contributions of this paper are summarized as follows. Firstly, the optimal open-loop Nash equilibrium is obtained in terms of the forward and backward stochastic difference equations (FBSDEs) by adopting the Pontryagin maximum principle. Secondly, a closed-loop Nash equilibrium to this local and remote stochastic nonzero-sum game for multiplicative noise system by using an orthogonal decomposition method is obtained. Finally, a simulation example is given to illustrate the validity of theoretical results.

articleTitle: H∞ Consensus of General Linear Multi-Agent Systems: A Dynamic Event-Triggered Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper addresses the leader-following $H_{\infty}$ consensus of linear multi-agent systems via distributed dynamic event-triggered control protocols. Both multi-agent systems with homogeneous and heterogeneous linear dynamics are considered. A novel dynamic event-triggering mechanism based on a unified time-and event-triggering framework is proposed. The open-loop estimation method is adopted to avoid continuous communication between neighboring agents. As a comparison, a static event-triggering mechanism is also studied in this work. It is shown that the $H_{\infty}$ consensus problem can be handled by the control protocols with the dynamic or static event-triggering mechanisms. At last, effectiveness of the proposed event-triggered control protocols are verified by two numerical examples, which shows that the dynamic event-triggering mechanism can further enlarge inter-event times.

articleTitle: Adaptive Prescribed Time Control for Quantized Nonlinear Systems with Time-Varying Parameters and Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the command filter-based adaptive prescribed time tracking control problem for the uncertain nonlinear systems with input quantization. By applying adaptive control technique to backstepping control framework, a compensation technique-based tracking control scheme is proposed, where the influence of unknown time-varying parameters and non-vanishing disturbances can be compensated. Different from some existing command filter-based asymptotic tracking control methods, the designed controller ensures the output tracking error converges to a preassigned residual set within the prescribed time. Finally, the simulation result is given to validate the effectiveness of the presented method.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoon in A Zero-Trust Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This work focuses on the constant time-distance platoon control problem of heterogeneous vehicle platoons in a zero-trust environment. The tracking error dynamics of each vehicle are constructed, and a constant time distance strategy based on the trust degree between vehicles is established in the zero-trust environment. Moreover, the asymptotic stability of the vehicle platoon when the communication topology is LPF is guaranteed. In addition, the precise feedback linearization technique is used to convert the vehicle dynamics model into a third-order linearization model, and the communication topology between vehicles is described using a directed graph. In particular, by designing a distributed controller, combined with directed graph and Routh-Hurwitz stability theorem, the stability condition of the gain of the distributed controller affected by trust under the LPF communication topology is proved. Finally, the obtained results are verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Learning-Based Fault-Tolerant Optimal Control for Spacecraft Constrained Reorientation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A fault-tolerant approximate optimal control law for constrained spacecraft attitude reorientation is proposed in this article, where both pointing and angular velocity constraints are taken into consideration. A judiciously designed term and two barrier functions are introduced into the reward function to cope with actuator faults and double-level state constraints. Then, adaptive dynamic programming approach is employed to solve the optimal problem online, wherein a single-critic neural network (NN) is developed within the framework of reinforcement learning. Specially, the concurrent learning method is incorporated into the NN update law to relax the excitation condition for error convergence. We prove in the Lyapunov sense that, the derived approximate optimal control policy can guarantee the boundedness of state and NN estimation error while satisfying pointing and angular velocity constraints, despite the presence of actuator faults. Numerical simulations are also presented to demonstrate our control scheme.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction and Accurate Localization Based on Hough Transform in Complex Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Complex industrial scenes, operation of large machinery or precision machinery, often need to judge, recognition and positioning of industrial scenes, to achieve intelligent systems to improve production efficiency. In view of the shortcomings of traditional manual recognition due to the fluctuation of subjective factors of operators, insufficient reliability, large variance of discnmination accuracy and low efficiency, and the need for a strong applicability system in combination with the variable relative distance between machinery operation and recognition objects, this study proposes a feature extraction and accurate positioning method based on Hough transform in complex scenes. This method reduces the noise interference and edge burr of the image by noise reduction filtering and feature extraction, and completes the feature extraction and accurate localization in complex scenes by introducing multiple relative threshold parameters. Finally, the method is put into work condition discrimination applications and real-time experiments are conducted. The experimental results prove that the Hough transform-based feature extraction and accurate positioning method in complex scenes is widely applicable, real-time, robust, low-cost and stable and reliable.

articleTitle: Blast furnace state monitoring method based on reliability analysis of sensing system
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Blast furnace (BF) ironmaking is a complex process with a series of devices, and failures occur from time to time. The accurate BF state monitoring is necessary and can effectively reduce the waste of resource and the occurrence of safety accidents. Currently, most data-driven BF state monitoring methods directly use the industrial field data collected by sensors, while less attention has been paid to the reliability of the data. This will reduce the accuracy of BF state monitoring, since data anomalies caused by kinds of sensor failures will directly lead to erroneous judgments of BF fault state. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a novel BF state monitoring method which takes the sensor states (failure or not) into account. In this method, an initial BF state monitoring model and a sensor state monitoring model are respectively constructed, mainly based on back propagation neural networks (BPNN). Afterwards, an online model is developed to coordinate the logical relationship between the initial BF state results and the sensor state results, to provide the final judgment of BF state. Validations on the dataset collected from a practical BF has shown that the BF state monitoring results is with an overall accuracy rate of 96.91%.

articleTitle: Multimode Process Monitoring Based on Density Space Clustering Locally Linear Embedding Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: To meet the demand for modern multimode processes, effective process monitoring techniques are needed to increase the quality of products and reduce safety hazards. In this article, a novel scheme based on density space clustering locally linear embedding (DBSLLE) strategy is proposed for multimode process monitoring. DBSLLE improves the monitoring performance of the locally linear embedding (LLE) method in multimode processes and overcomes the difficulty of new samples unable to be projected by the LLE method. The basic idea of the proposed method is first adopting the density based space clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) rule to eliminate the multimode structure; next, the conventional LLE is used to extract nonlinear features from each model data and achieve dimensionality reduction. Finally, the weighted average distance sum of square is constructed as a statistic to monitor the process. The new sample is determined to belong to which model based on the sample density of the space in which it resides; A cost function is constructed between the new sample and the samples in its model, and the weight matrix is obtained by minimizing it; The weight matrix is multiplied with the low-dimensional projection of the training data to obtain the projection of the new sample; The statistical value of the projection sample is calculated to obtain the current state of the process. The efficiency of the proposed monitoring scheme is implemented in a multimode numerical simulation case, Tennessee-Eastman processes, and in the Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR). The experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms the traditional LLE monitoring schemes.

articleTitle: Distributed Fault Detection Scheme for Intelligent Connected Vehicles in a Zero-trust Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the analysis and design of distributed fault detection for $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ observer-based intelligent connected vehicles in a zero-trust environment. Intelligent connected vehicles can improve traffic efficiency, but the system can be unreliable due to network security issues. Fault detection of intelligent connected vehicles is performed by introducing a zero-trust paradigm. First, the relative output estimation error is defined based on the communication topology of the intelligent connected vehicle. Then, a design scheme of $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ observer-based fault detection for the distributed system of intelligent connected vehicles in a zero-trust environment is proposed, and the stability and existence conditions of the observer for the distributed system of intelligent connected vehicles are verified. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the design scheme are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Software-in-the-Loop Simulation of Cooperative Fixed-wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper develops a software-in-the-loop (SITL) simulation platform for fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to test the cooperative control algorithms. The platform is based on ROS, Gazebo and PX4 SITL to realize the visualized simulation of multiple fixed-wing UAVs. The architecture consists of five layers including communication layer, simulator layer, flight control layer, coordination layer and human interaction layer. The control inputs and outputs are packaged as topics and services under the ROS communication network. To accomplish the cooperative control of fixed-wing UAVs, we design a two-loop control scheme, which consists of the PX4 inner-loop attitude controller, and the proposed outer-loop cooperative controller. A simulation is presented which incorporates the cooperative path-following control and leader-following control to achieve the cooperative behavior of four UAVs.

articleTitle: Adaptive model reference tracking for high-order nonlinear time-varying systems with time-varying delays: A fully actuated system approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the adaptive model reference tracking (AMRT) problem for a general high-order nonlinear time-varying system with time-varying delays and unknown constant parameters is investigated by applying the fully actuated system (FAS) approach. An adaptive controller is designed for the high-order nonlinear system based on the Lyapunov stability theory. With the obtained adaptive control results, an AMRT controller is proposed to ensure that the tracking error system is asymptotically stable and the unknown parameter estimation error is bounded. The established AMRT controller is composed of three parts, the basic part cancels the known nonlinearities in the system and simultaneously assigns the linear dominant term in the closed-loop system, the adaptive part overcomes the effects of unknown constant parameters, the compensator part compensates the effect of the reference model state vector and control input to the tracking error. Based on the parametric solution to the Sylvester matrix equation, a complete parametric form of the AMRT controller is given. An application to spacecraft attitude system indicates satisfactory control system performances with the proposed AMRT scheme.

articleTitle: The Design of Adaptive Integrated Guidance and Control Subjected to State Constraints and Multiple Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper focuses on adaptive dynamic surface composite control subjected to state constraints and multiple uncertainties in integrated guidance and control (IGC) design for skid-to-turn missiles. The novel IGC algorithm incorporates adaptive dynamic surface composite control with the barrier Lyapunov function. Composite control in this paper takes a superior approach by introducing the estimated information of the system states from the series-parallel estimation model into the neural network under the framework of adaptive dynamic surface control to achieve composite learning, which makes the algorithm learn more accurately for system disturbance. Meanwhile, the saturation function and the barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) ensure that the system state satisfies the constraints. The effectiveness of the IGC scheme is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control for Attitude and Altitude Synchronization of Quadrotors Based on Fully-Actuated System Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed fault-tolerant synchronization control scheme, which utilizes a distributed observer to estimate the state of a virtual leader and fully-actuated system approaches to address actuator faults in a multiagent quadrotor system. Additionally, in the process of linearizing using the fully-actuated system method, a tracking differentiator is introduced to provide reference signals and their derivatives for the system. The fault-tolerant control algorithm based on the fully-actuated system method guarantees asymptotic convergence of the altitude and attitude tracking errors, even in the presence of actuator faults. Finally, the numerical simulation is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed fault-tolerant synchronization control algorithm.

articleTitle: Hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture for carrier airwake prediction using attention in frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The carrier airwake is the result of ocean air flowing across the stern of a moving aircraft carrier. This airwake has a huge impact on how accurately a carrier-based aircraft can land. If it is possible to make accurate predictions for the future carrier airwake, the predicted results will be used to aid the landing process and ensure a more precise landing. In this study, the properties of the carrier airwake are first analyzed to provide a basis for the subsequent design of the neural network. Then we propose a hierarchical encoder-decoder neural network with an attention mechanism in the frequency domain to simultaneously predict the carrier airwake components in all directions. Finally, the full comprehensive experiments show that our model for predicting the carrier airwake is accurate.

articleTitle: GAU-Net: U-Net Variant for Segmentation of Skin Lesion
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: Image segmentation of skin lesions is a critical component in the auxiliary diagnosis of medical-related diseases. However, traditional U-Net network methods struggle to achieve accurate segmentation results when presented with high-resolution skin lesion images, especially under small batch size training conditions. In this study, we propose a novel GAU-Net network that leverages the attention mechanism of mobile networks. Based on U-Net, the method employs Group Normalization and LeakyReLU activation functions in the convolution block to obtain normalized and reliable features, thereby enhancing the network’s ability to represent high-level semantic information. Additionally, the proposed method introduces Coordinate Attention to embed effective position information into the channel Attention, further improving the model’s segmentation results. We evaluated the segmentation performance of GAU-Net on the ISIC2016 skin disease dataset, showing that it outperformed traditional segmentation indicators such as mIoU and mAP. These results demonstrate the superiority of GAU-Net as an effective solution for skin lesion image segmentation.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Mean-Field Linear Quadratic Control with Partial System Information
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, the infinite horizon linear quadratic (LQ) optimal control problem for mean-field systems with partial system information is solved by using the reinforcement learning (RL) approach. Although the introduction of the mean-field terms in system dynamics and the cost function will destroy the adaptiveness of the control law, the optimal stabilization control is derived based on the proposed online RL algorithm and the Bellman dynamic programming. Moreover, the proposed algorithm requires only the local state data of the mean-field system to compute the optimal control, and the stepwise stability of the stabilizers is shown. Finally, numerical example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive Position Tracking Control of Uncertain Stewart Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a parameter adaptive sliding mode control algorithm to address the generalized position tracking control issue for a Stewart Platform in the presence of parametric uncertainties and external disturbances. First, nonlinear dynamic equations of the Stewart Platform are extracted by the Lagrange method. To improve the performance of the conventional sliding mode control method, the parameter adaptive technique is applied to estimate the switching gain, which not only reduces the chattering phenomenon, but also avoids the conservatism of the controller. A rigorous stability analysis is given to prove that the tracking errors are uniformly ultimately bounded by Lyapunov stability theory. Numerical simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fixed-Time Consensus Control for Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems with Input Quantization and Dead-Zone
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This article investigates the fixed-time tracking control problem of second-order multi-agent systems with input quantization, external disturbances as well as dead-zone nonlinearity. By employing a nonlinear decomposition between the system input and the control signal, the major difficulty for the coupling between the quantized input and dead-zone nonlinearity is resolved. Based on this, an adaptive fixed-time consensus control algorithm is designed by utilizing the technique of adding a power integrator. The proposed control law needs no information about the parameters of the quantizers and the upper bounds of dead-zone parameters. Rigorous proofs show that the tracking errors can reach a small set near zero within a preassigned time, where the settling time has no connection with the initial conditions of agents. Therefore, it is possible to off-line preassign the convergence time according to the requirement of task.

articleTitle: Distributed prescribed-time fault-tolerant attitude tracking control for multiple rigid spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, distributed prescribed-time fault-tolerant attitude tracking control problem for multiple spacecraft is investigated under a directed communication topology. Each follower spacecraft is subject to unknown nonidentical and unpredictable actuation faults. By using time transformation approach, a distributed prescribed-time attitude tracking protocol is designed for each follower to track the states of the leader. By using the uniformly bounded time-varying gains, the numerical implementation problem arising from infinite time-varying gain is avoided, and the prescribed time can be determined in advance, irrespective of the initial conditions of the followers, which is deemed favorable in practice. Simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the developed distributed attitude control scheme.

articleTitle: Adaptive finite-time sliding mode attitude tracking control laws for flexible spacecraft with actuator saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: In this paper, attitude tracking control for flexible spacecraft with inertia uncertainty, disturbance and actuator saturation is investigated. First, a switching function is constructed by using attitude velocity tracking errors and quaternion errors. Then, an adaptive finite-time sliding mode controller is derived for the flexible spacecraft to guarantee that the control goals can still be achieved when actuator saturation happens. To verify the effectiveness of the presented control laws, simulations are performed for a flexible spacecraft in the presence of inertia uncertainty, disturbance and actuator saturation. In addition, some existing control strategies are compared with the presented adaptive finite-time sliding mode control laws to demonstrate the superior control performance of the proposed control schemes.

articleTitle: Decentralized tracking control for high-speed train: A fully actuated system approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: To implement a smoother automatic train operation (ATO) for high-speed train (HST), we investigates the classical tracking problem for the cascaded mass-point longitudinal model of HST with train schedule, which is subject to the constraints of speed and power. The most challenge is the existence of nonlinear coupler forces between front and rear cars. In this paper, we introduce the fully actuated system approaches to remove the coupler forces from the train dynamic model, and then the second-order full-actuation system is established for each car. Therefore the decentralized controller of the individual car can be easy to been designed. In addition, the sufficient conditions for the existence of the decentralized controller are given by a set of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Some simulation results show the effectiveness of the fully actuated system approaches, and then the control scheme ensures the consensus of the relative displacement and velocity of coupler.

articleTitle: Terminal Orbital Adaptive Dynamic Programming-based Control for Satellite Pursuit Evasion Game with Input Saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: A continuous space pursuit-evasion game algorithm based on zero-sum game is proposed to solve the problem of the terminal pursuit-evasion control of spacecraft with input saturation. A novel single-network adaptive dynamic programming method is proposed to obtain the solution of zero-sum game. Firstly, it is assumed that the two satellites are close such that the nonlinear dynamics could be reduced to the CW equations. Considering the input saturation, a non-quadratic cost function is proposed to formulate a Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation. Then, only a critic neural network is employed to learn the optimal value function and further obtain the optimal controller, which enables the architecture of adaptive dynamic programming implementation to be simpler. An NN weight updating law is constructed, by which the restriction of initial admissible control is removed. Based on the Lyapunov theory, the convergence of critic NN weights and the stability of closed-loop system are guaranteed. Finally, numerical results verify the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Observer-Based Consensus Control for Nonlinear Leader-Following Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper studies the prescribed-time consensus control problem of the nonlinear leader-following multi-agent systems(MASs). The convergence time of our protocol can be set according to the needs of the actual task. In the leader-following model, we construct a distributed prescribed-time observer(DPTO) to reconstruct the leader’s state, so that the leader’s information can be accurately obtained by followers. Then we designed a tracking controller to make each follower’s state consistent with the restructureed leader’s state. Finally, the simulation verifies that the control protocol proposed by us is feasible.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Pose Tracking Control for Multiple Spacecraft Rendezvous with Collision Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of position tracking and attitude synchronization for multiple chaser spacecraft rendezvous and docking with the target spacecraft, in which model uncertainties, unknown external disturbances, path constraints, and collision avoidance are considered. The coupled six-degrees-of-freedom (6DOF) dynamic model is adopted for spacecraft relative motion. By integrating the artificial potential function (APF), a 6DOF robust adaptive controller is designed. In addition, unknown parameters are estimated with a norm-estimation-based adaptive method. The stability of the system is proved by Lyapunov theory and a simulation example is given to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Cable Tension Distribution Methods of Cable Driven Serpentine Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (CFASTA)
abstract: The cable-driven serpentine manipulator has shown great application value in many fields due to its excellent compliance and flexibility. Most of the existing cable-driven serpentine manipulator adopts the position control mode, and the length of the driving cable is unique when the joint angle is determined, but the cable tension can be changed, that is, the cable tension is not unique. unreasonable cable tension can reduce the positioning accuracy of the manipulator and even damage the structure. This paper introduces six cable tension distribution methods to analyze the static equilibrium workspace of the cable-driven serpentine manipulator and compare them with the kinematic workspace. The results show that the cable tension distribution method has a great impact on the static equilibrium workspace of the cable-driven serpentine manipulator. The static equilibrium workspace under the numerical algorithm is much greater than the analytical algorithm, but the calculation speed is far less than that of the analytical algorithm. This paper has a certain reference value for selecting a suitable cable tension distribution method to expand the static equilibrium workspace and improve the working range and control accuracy of the cable-driven serpentine manipulator.
